spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m7p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A subway block's occupant record is updated via compare-and-swap (CAS):
\* a controller reads the version, decides a candidate value, and its later
\* commit is accepted only if the version is unchanged (otherwise it is
\* correctly rejected as stale). A privileged admin may override the record
\* at any time, bypassing the compare check, but still advances the version
\* so stale controller commits are still correctly rejected afterward.
\* The invariant protects against a controller ever committing -- and
\* thereby silently discarding someone else's update -- on a stale read.

CONSTANTS Controllers, Trains, AdminC, NoneC, NoneT, NoneV, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, occupant, observed, proposal, lastWriter, lastWriteVersion

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in Nat
    /\ occupant \in Trains \cup {NoneT}
    /\ observed \in [Controllers -> Nat \cup {NoneV}]
    /\ proposal \in [Controllers -> Trains \cup {NoneT}]
    /\ lastWriter \in Controllers \cup {AdminC, NoneC}
    /\ lastWriteVersion \in Nat

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ occupant = NoneT
    /\ observed = [c \in Controllers |-> NoneV]
    /\ proposal = [c \in Controllers |-> NoneT]
    /\ lastWriter = NoneC
    /\ lastWriteVersion = 0

\* A controller with no pending attempt snapshots the version and decides
\* on a candidate occupant to propose.
Read(c) ==
    /\ observed[c] = NoneV
    /\ \E t \in Trains \cup {NoneT} :
        /\ observed' = [observed EXCEPT ![c] = version]
        /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![c] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, version, lastWriter, lastWriteVersion>>

\* CAS accepted: the controller's snapshot still matches the current
\* version, so its candidate commits and the version advances.
CasSucceed(c) ==
    /\ observed[c] # NoneV
    /\ observed[c] = version
    /\ occupant' = proposal[c]
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ lastWriter' = c
    /\ lastWriteVersion' = observed[c]
    /\ observed' = [observed EXCEPT ![c] = NoneV]
    /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![c] = NoneT]

\* CAS rejected: the snapshot is stale, so nothing about the record
\* changes and the controller must re-read before retrying.
CasStale(c) ==
    /\ observed[c] # NoneV
    /\ observed[c] # version
    /\ observed' = [observed EXCEPT ![c] = NoneV]
    /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![c] = NoneT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, version, lastWriter, lastWriteVersion>>

\* A controller abandons a pending attempt without writing.
CancelRead(c) ==
    /\ observed[c] # NoneV
    /\ observed' = [observed EXCEPT ![c] = NoneV]
    /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![c] = NoneT]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<occupant, version, lastWriter, lastWriteVersion>>

\* The privileged admin overrides the record, ignoring any comparison,
\* but still advances the version so later stale commits are rejected.
AdminOverride ==
    /\ \E t \in Trains \cup {NoneT} :
        /\ occupant' = t
        /\ version' = version + 1
        /\ lastWriter' = AdminC
        /\ lastWriteVersion' = version
    /\ UNCHANGED <<observed, proposal>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : Read(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : CasSucceed(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : CasStale(c)
    \/ \E c \in Controllers : CancelRead(c)
    \/ AdminOverride

vars == <<version, occupant, observed, proposal, lastWriter, lastWriteVersion>>

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A c \in Controllers : WF_vars(CasSucceed(c) \/ CasStale(c) \/ CancelRead(c))

\* SAFETY: no controller ever commits -- silently discarding a concurrent
\* update -- on a stale read.
NoLostUpdates ==
    (lastWriter \in Controllers) => (lastWriteVersion = version - 1)

\* LIVENESS: every pending read is eventually resolved one way or another.
EveryReadEventuallyResolves ==
    \A c \in Controllers : (observed[c] # NoneV) ~> (observed[c] = NoneV)

\* Keeps the reachable state space finite for model checking.
StateConstraint == version <= MaxVersion

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2}
    Trains = {t1, t2}
    AdminC = admin
    NoneC = nonec
    NoneT = nonet
    NoneV = nonev
    MaxVersion = 4
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
PROPERTY EveryReadEventuallyResolves
CONSTRAINT StateConstraint
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A subway line's signalling system keeps one shared record per track block describing which train (if any) currently occupies that block. Several trackside signalling controllers may propose changing the block's occupant, but they must not silently clobber each other's updates: each controller first reads the block record's current version number and decides on a new occupant value, then later attempts to commit that value with a compare-and-swap (CAS) -- the commit is accepted only if the version has not changed since the controller's read, and is otherwise rejected as stale so the controller must re-read and retry. A privileged control-center admin can also override the block record directly at any time, without needing to have read a matching version first, for emergencies such as forcing a block clear; every admin write still advances the version number so any controller whose earlier read is now stale will correctly have its own commit rejected rather than overwriting the admin's action.

The system's actions are: (1) Read -- a controller with no pending attempt reads the block record's current version and decides on a candidate new occupant (a specific train, or nobody); (2) CasSucceed -- a controller whose pending read version still equals the block record's current version commits its candidate occupant, which becomes the new record value, and the version advances by one; (3) CasStale -- a controller whose pending read version no longer equals the current version has its attempt rejected: no change is made to the record, and the controller's pending attempt is cleared so it can re-read; (4) CancelRead -- a controller with a pending read simply abandons it (whether or not it was still fresh) without writing, clearing its pending attempt; (5) AdminOverride -- the privileged admin sets the block record to any occupant value at any time, bypassing the compare check entirely, and the version still advances by one.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, whenever the most recent successful write to the block record was made by an ordinary controller (not the admin), the version number that controller had read before committing is exactly one less than the record's current version -- meaning no controller ever successfully commits, and thereby loses another update, on the basis of a stale read.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every controller that has a pending read attempt on the block record eventually resolves it -- either by successfully committing its candidate occupant, having its stale attempt correctly rejected, or cancelling -- so no controller's signalling request is ever left permanently pending, even though the admin may repeatedly override the record out from under it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od11m7p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Workers, Jobs, NoneW

\* owner[j] is a compare-and-swap register: Claim CAS-es it NoneW -> w,
\* Reclaim CAS-es it crashedWorker -> NoneW. printCount[j] is a second CAS
\* register that Print CAS-es 0 -> 1; since that CAS can only ever succeed
\* once per job (its own guard requires printCount[j] = 0), the irreversible
\* physical print action can never happen twice, even across a crash and a
\* subsequent reclaim/reassignment to a different worker.
VARIABLES waiting, owner, printCount, crashedWorker, archived

TypeOK == waiting \subseteq Jobs /\ owner \in [Jobs -> Workers \cup {NoneW}]
          /\ printCount \in [Jobs -> Nat] /\ crashedWorker \in Workers \cup {NoneW}
          /\ archived \subseteq Jobs

Init == waiting = Jobs /\ owner = [j \in Jobs |-> NoneW]
        /\ printCount = [j \in Jobs |-> 0] /\ crashedWorker = NoneW
        /\ archived = {}

\* Release a job from the intake pile into the active spool.
Spool(j) == j \in waiting /\ waiting' = waiting \ {j}
            /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, printCount, crashedWorker, archived>>

\* CAS: owner register goes NoneW -> w, only for a spooled, unowned,
\* not-yet-printed job, and only for a worker not already holding another.
Claim(w, j) == w # crashedWorker /\ j \notin waiting
               /\ owner[j] = NoneW /\ printCount[j] = 0
               /\ (\A j2 \in Jobs: owner[j2] # w)
               /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = w]
               /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, printCount, crashedWorker, archived>>

\* CAS: print counter goes 0 -> 1 -- the irreversible action, at most once.
Print(w, j) == w # crashedWorker /\ owner[j] = w /\ printCount[j] = 0
               /\ printCount' = [printCount EXCEPT ![j] = printCount[j] + 1]
               /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = NoneW]
               /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, crashedWorker, archived>>

\* Exactly one worker, ever, may crash silently, freezing its held job.
Crash(w) == crashedWorker = NoneW /\ crashedWorker' = w
            /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, owner, printCount, archived>>

\* CAS: owner register goes crashedWorker -> NoneW, only if not yet printed.
Reclaim(j) == crashedWorker # NoneW /\ owner[j] = crashedWorker
              /\ printCount[j] = 0
              /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![j] = NoneW]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, printCount, crashedWorker, archived>>

\* A physically printed job is later filed into the shop's completed-jobs
\* archive -- a genuinely separate clerical step after printing that can
\* never affect whether a job gets printed, so it cannot stall progress.
Archive(j) == printCount[j] = 1 /\ j \notin archived
              /\ archived' = archived \cup {j}
              /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, owner, printCount, crashedWorker>>

ClaimAny(j) == \E w \in Workers: Claim(w, j)
PrintAny(j) == \E w \in Workers: Print(w, j)

Next == (\E j \in Jobs: Spool(j)) \/ (\E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs: Claim(w, j))
        \/ (\E w \in Workers, j \in Jobs: Print(w, j))
        \/ (\E w \in Workers: Crash(w)) \/ (\E j \in Jobs: Reclaim(j))
        \/ (\E j \in Jobs: Archive(j))

vars == <<waiting, owner, printCount, crashedWorker, archived>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ (\A j \in Jobs: WF_vars(Spool(j)))
        /\ (\A j \in Jobs: SF_vars(ClaimAny(j)))
        /\ (\A j \in Jobs: WF_vars(PrintAny(j)))
        /\ (\A j \in Jobs: WF_vars(Reclaim(j)))

\* SAFETY: the irreversible print action fires at most once per job.
AtMostOncePrinted == \A j \in Jobs: printCount[j] <= 1

\* LIVENESS: every job is eventually printed, exactly once.
AllEventuallyPrinted == <>(\A j \in Jobs: printCount[j] = 1)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2}
    Jobs = {j1, j2, j3}
    NoneW = none
INVARIANT AtMostOncePrinted
PROPERTY AllEventuallyPrinted
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A neighborhood print shop runs several printer workers off one job spooler.
Every job starts out sitting in an intake pile before it is released into the
shop's active spool. Once released, ownership of a job is protected by a
compare-and-swap register: a printer worker may only become a job's owner by
successfully CAS-ing the job's owner register from "unowned" to itself, which
only succeeds if no other worker currently owns that job. Actually printing a
job -- ink physically hitting paper -- is a separate, irreversible action
that a worker may only perform while it owns the job, and it too is guarded
by a compare-and-swap: the worker CAS-es the job's print counter from 0 to 1,
which can only ever succeed once per job, so a given job can never be
physically printed a second time.

The twist is that a printer worker can crash silently at any moment,
including while it currently owns a job it has not yet printed. A crashed
worker does nothing further -- it never prints and never claims another job.
So the shop does not stall forever, a reclaim step notices a job still owned
by the crashed worker that has not yet been printed and CAS-es its owner
register back to "unowned" (expected value: the crashed worker) so a
different, still-working worker can claim it and finish the job. Reclaim only
ever touches a job that has not yet been printed, so it can never itself
cause a job to be printed twice.

The full action set is:
  - Spool(j): a job j sitting in the intake pile is released into the active
    spool, making it eligible for a worker to claim.
  - Claim(w, j): a non-crashed worker w that does not currently own any other
    job successfully CAS-es ownership of a spooled, unowned, not-yet-printed
    job j to itself.
  - Print(w, j): a non-crashed worker w that owns job j CAS-es the job's
    print counter from 0 to 1, irreversibly printing it, and then releases
    its ownership of the job.
  - Crash(w): at most one worker, chosen nondeterministically, crashes
    silently, freezing whatever job (if any) it currently owns.
  - Reclaim(j): a job j still owned by the crashed worker, and not yet
    printed, has its owner register CAS-ed back to "unowned" so another
    worker can take it over.
  - Archive(j): a job j that has already been physically printed is filed
    into the shop's completed-jobs archive, a separate clerical bookkeeping
    step that happens strictly after printing and can never affect whether
    or how many times a job gets printed.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every job, its print counter never exceeds 1 -- no job
is ever physically printed more than once.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every job that starts out in the intake pile is eventually
printed exactly once, even though the worker that first claims it may crash
silently before finishing it.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m2p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A regional blood-bank slot is allocated via two-phase commit across a
\* fixed set of participant hospitals. At most one hospital may crash
\* silently, and permanently, mid-round. Commit is only legal once every
\* still-live hospital has voted YES and no crash occurred during the round;
\* otherwise the round must abort. The invariant protects against the slot
\* ever being recorded COMMITTED on the basis of an incomplete or tainted
\* round (no double allocation of the same slot).

CONSTANT Participants

VARIABLES status, voted, crashed, crashedDuringRound

TypeOK ==
    /\ status \in {"Available", "Prepare", "Committed"}
    /\ voted \subseteq Participants
    /\ crashed \subseteq Participants
    /\ crashedDuringRound \in BOOLEAN

Init ==
    /\ status = "Available"
    /\ voted = {}
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ crashedDuringRound = FALSE

\* Begin a fresh allocation round for the (idle) slot.
StartRound ==
    /\ status = "Available"
    /\ status' = "Prepare"
    /\ voted' = {}
    /\ crashedDuringRound' = FALSE
    /\ UNCHANGED crashed

\* A live, not-yet-voted participant casts a YES vote for the current round.
Vote ==
    /\ status = "Prepare"
    /\ \E p \in (Participants \ voted) \ crashed :
        voted' = voted \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, crashed, crashedDuringRound>>

\* At most one participant ever crashes, silently, before it has voted.
CrashParticipant ==
    /\ status = "Prepare"
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ \E p \in Participants \ voted :
        crashed' = {p}
    /\ crashedDuringRound' = TRUE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<status, voted>>

\* Commit is legal only once every still-live participant has voted YES
\* and no crash tainted this round.
Commit ==
    /\ status = "Prepare"
    /\ voted = Participants \ crashed
    /\ ~crashedDuringRound
    /\ status' = "Committed"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<voted, crashed, crashedDuringRound>>

\* A crash-tainted round must abort; the slot returns to available.
Abort ==
    /\ status = "Prepare"
    /\ crashedDuringRound
    /\ status' = "Available"
    /\ voted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, crashedDuringRound>>

\* A committed slot is eventually released back to the pool.
Release ==
    /\ status = "Committed"
    /\ status' = "Available"
    /\ voted' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, crashedDuringRound>>

Next == StartRound \/ Vote \/ CrashParticipant \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ Release

vars == <<status, voted, crashed, crashedDuringRound>>

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Vote)
    /\ WF_vars(Commit)
    /\ WF_vars(Abort)
    /\ WF_vars(Release)

\* SAFETY: a COMMITTED slot's recorded round is always complete and untainted.
NoDoubleAllocation ==
    status = "Committed" => (voted = Participants \ crashed /\ ~crashedDuringRound)

\* LIVENESS: every started round eventually resolves, and every commit is
\* eventually released so the slot can be reused.
AllRoundsEventuallyResolve ==
    /\ (status = "Prepare") ~> (status \in {"Committed", "Available"})
    /\ (status = "Committed") ~> (status = "Available")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Participants = {h1, h2, h3}
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
PROPERTY AllRoundsEventuallyResolve
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A regional blood-bank network keeps a shared inventory of blood-unit slots that hospitals reserve for transfusions. A coordinator drives a two-phase commit protocol across a fixed set of participant hospitals whenever a slot needs to be allocated to a patient request: the coordinator first asks every participant to vote (PREPARE), and only when all participants have voted YES does the coordinator move the slot to COMMITTED and allocate it; if the coordinator instead decides to ABORT, the slot returns to available. One of the participant hospitals can crash silently at any point in the protocol -- once crashed it stops casting further votes for the round it was in, but the coordinator can still (eventually) resolve the round: it may only commit a round if every participant, including one that later turns out to be unresponsive, actually voted YES before the crash, and it must abort any round in which a participant crashed before voting. After a round resolves (commit or abort) the coordinator moves on and a fresh round can start for the slot, using the remaining live participants. The protocol never runs two overlapping allocation rounds for the same slot, and a slot that is already COMMITTED can never be entered into a new round or be allocated again until it is explicitly released back to the pool.

The system's actions are: (1) StartRound -- the coordinator begins a new two-phase-commit round for the slot when it is idle/available, moving the round phase to PREPARE and clearing prior votes; (2) Vote -- a live (non-crashed) participant that has not yet voted in the current round casts a YES vote; (3) CrashParticipant -- a designated participant that has not yet voted in the current round crashes silently, after which it can cast no further votes for that round; (4) Commit -- the coordinator commits the round and allocates the slot, but only when every participant has voted YES and none has crashed during the round; (5) Abort -- the coordinator aborts the round, returning the slot to available, whenever a participant has crashed before voting in that round (or the coordinator otherwise gives up on the round); (6) Release -- once a slot is COMMITTED (allocated), it is eventually released back to available, clearing the round state so a fresh round can start.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the slot is never simultaneously recorded as COMMITTED/allocated by more than one two-phase-commit round -- concretely, whenever the slot's status is COMMITTED, the round's vote record shows that every participant voted YES and no participant crashed during that round, so the same slot is never allocated on the basis of two different or incomplete rounds (no double allocation).
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every two-phase-commit round that is started for the slot is eventually resolved -- it eventually reaches either COMMITTED (with the slot allocated) or is aborted and the slot returns to available -- even though one participant may crash silently partway through, and every COMMITTED slot is eventually released so future rounds can proceed.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od12m8p2t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Movers, FridgesPerRegion, Total, NoneM, NoneF

\* Hierarchical locking: a mover first takes a coarse region lock, then fine
\* fridge locks inside that region, before it may move one blood unit. One
\* courier may be arbitrarily slow between acquiring locks and transferring,
\* but every mover that starts eventually finishes and releases its locks.
\* The safety invariant protects total blood volume (nothing created/lost);
\* the liveness property protects forward progress despite the slow courier.
Regions == {1, 2}
Fridges == Regions \X (1..FridgesPerRegion)
FridgeHome == <<1, 1>>

VARIABLES regionLock, fridgeLock, units, phase, src, dst

vars == <<regionLock, fridgeLock, units, phase, src, dst>>

FridgesInRegion(rg) == {f \in Fridges : f[1] = rg}

RECURSIVE SumUnits(_)
SumUnits(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
               ELSE LET f == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                    IN units[f] + SumUnits(S \ {f})

\* All units start in one fridge; a total ordering is unnecessary because
\* the exact starting distribution does not matter to either property.
Init == regionLock = [rg \in Regions |-> NoneM]
        /\ fridgeLock = [f \in Fridges |-> NoneM]
        /\ units = [f \in Fridges |-> IF f = FridgeHome THEN Total ELSE 0]
        /\ phase = [m \in Movers |-> "idle"]
        /\ src = [m \in Movers |-> NoneF]
        /\ dst = [m \in Movers |-> NoneF]

AcquireRegion(m) == phase[m] = "idle"
    /\ \E rg \in Regions :
         regionLock[rg] = NoneM
         /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![rg] = m]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "hasRegion"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fridgeLock, units, src, dst>>

AcquireFridges(m) == phase[m] = "hasRegion"
    /\ \E rg \in Regions :
         regionLock[rg] = m
         /\ \E f1, f2 \in FridgesInRegion(rg) :
              f1 # f2 /\ fridgeLock[f1] = NoneM /\ fridgeLock[f2] = NoneM
              /\ fridgeLock' = [fridgeLock EXCEPT ![f1] = m, ![f2] = m]
              /\ src' = [src EXCEPT ![m] = f1]
              /\ dst' = [dst EXCEPT ![m] = f2]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "hasFridges"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, units>>

\* AttemptTransfer always fires once fridges are locked: if the source
\* fridge is empty the mover simply finds nothing to move (a genuine,
\* always-enabled outcome), which keeps the courier from ever being stuck
\* waiting on a source that can never refill without violating conservation.
AttemptTransfer(m) == phase[m] = "hasFridges"
    /\ \/ /\ units[src[m]] > 0
          /\ units' = [units EXCEPT ![src[m]] = @ - 1, ![dst[m]] = @ + 1]
       \/ /\ units[src[m]] = 0
          /\ units' = units
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "transferred"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<regionLock, fridgeLock, src, dst>>

Release(m) == phase[m] = "transferred"
    /\ \E rg \in Regions :
         regionLock[rg] = m
         /\ regionLock' = [regionLock EXCEPT ![rg] = NoneM]
    /\ fridgeLock' = [fridgeLock EXCEPT ![src[m]] = NoneM, ![dst[m]] = NoneM]
    /\ phase' = [phase EXCEPT ![m] = "idle"]
    /\ src' = [src EXCEPT ![m] = NoneF]
    /\ dst' = [dst EXCEPT ![m] = NoneF]
    /\ UNCHANGED units

Next == (\E m \in Movers : AcquireRegion(m))
        \/ (\E m \in Movers : AcquireFridges(m))
        \/ (\E m \in Movers : AttemptTransfer(m))
        \/ (\E m \in Movers : Release(m))

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ \A m \in Movers : WF_vars(AcquireFridges(m)) /\ WF_vars(AttemptTransfer(m)) /\ WF_vars(Release(m))

UnitsConserved == SumUnits(Fridges) = Total

AllAcquirersEventuallyRelease == \A m \in Movers : (phase[m] = "hasRegion") ~> (phase[m] = "idle")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Movers = {m1, m2}
    FridgesPerRegion = 2
    Total = 3
    NoneM = noneM
    NoneF = noneF
INVARIANT UnitsConserved
PROPERTY AllAcquirersEventuallyRelease
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A regional blood bank tracks units of a single blood type as they move between a small set of storage fridges. To move a unit between two fridges the bank uses hierarchical locking: a mover must first acquire a coarse region lock (there are two regions, each covering a fixed subset of the fridges) and only then acquire a fine-grained lock on the specific source fridge and the specific destination fridge inside that region, before the transfer of one unit can actually happen. Every fridge belongs to exactly one region. One of the bank's couriers can be slow -- it may take an arbitrarily long time between acquiring its locks and completing the transfer step -- but it never crashes or drops its locks; it always eventually finishes what it started, it just cannot be assumed to hurry. The full action set is: (1) AcquireRegion -- a mover with no locks held acquires the coarse lock for one of the two regions, provided no other mover currently holds that region lock; (2) AcquireFridges -- a mover holding a region lock (and no fridge locks yet) picks a distinct source fridge and destination fridge that both belong to that locked region and acquires the fine-grained locks on both, provided neither fridge is currently fine-locked by another mover; (3) AttemptTransfer -- a mover holding both fine-grained fridge locks attempts to move one unit of blood from its locked source fridge to its locked destination fridge: if the source fridge currently holds at least one unit, exactly one unit moves across from the source fridge's count to the destination fridge's count, and if the source fridge happens to be empty, nothing moves but the mover's attempt still completes (this keeps a courier from being stuck forever waiting on a source that can never refill); (4) Release -- a mover that has completed its transfer attempt releases both its fine-grained fridge locks and its region lock, returning to holding no locks at all, so a new AcquireRegion can start its next move. The total number of blood units summed across all fridges is fixed and never changes, no matter how many transfer attempts occur, because AttemptTransfer only ever moves a unit from one fridge's count to another fridge's count (or moves nothing at all) -- it never creates or destroys a unit. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the sum of blood units held across all fridges equals the fixed total number of units the blood bank started with. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every mover that acquires a region lock eventually completes its transfer and releases all of its locks, even if that mover is the slow courier that is never assumed to act quickly.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od13m4p4t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Machines, Capacity, MaxCredit, MaxRefills

\* Bounded work queue with backpressure: machines spend local credit to
\* send, but the network (modeled as an unordered set, not a channel) may
\* reorder deliveries, so a machine's credit can be stale. QueueWithinCapacity
\* protects the fact that the depot's own admission check at delivery time
\* -- not the machines' credit bookkeeping -- is what keeps the queue bounded.
VARIABLES queue, inflightReq, credit, refillBudget

vars == <<queue, inflightReq, credit, refillBudget>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ queue \in Seq(Machines)
    /\ Len(queue) <= Capacity
    /\ inflightReq \subseteq Machines
    /\ credit \in [Machines -> 0..MaxCredit]
    /\ refillBudget \in 0..MaxRefills

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ inflightReq = {}
    /\ credit = [m \in Machines |-> MaxCredit]
    /\ refillBudget = MaxRefills

\* A machine with credit and no outstanding request puts one on the network.
SendRequest(m) ==
    /\ credit[m] > 0
    /\ m \notin inflightReq
    /\ credit' = [credit EXCEPT ![m] = @ - 1]
    /\ inflightReq' = inflightReq \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, refillBudget>>

\* Reordered delivery of an in-flight request that finds room: admitted.
DeliverAdmit(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflightReq
    /\ Len(queue) < Capacity
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, m)
    /\ inflightReq' = inflightReq \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<credit, refillBudget>>

\* Reordered delivery that finds the queue full: backpressure drops it.
DeliverReject(m) ==
    /\ m \in inflightReq
    /\ Len(queue) = Capacity
    /\ inflightReq' = inflightReq \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, credit, refillBudget>>

\* The depot's worker services and removes the oldest admitted job.
ProcessQueue ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<inflightReq, credit, refillBudget>>

\* The depot grants back one unit of credit, out of its shared, finite budget.
RefillCredit(m) ==
    /\ refillBudget > 0
    /\ credit[m] < MaxCredit
    /\ credit' = [credit EXCEPT ![m] = @ + 1]
    /\ refillBudget' = refillBudget - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, inflightReq>>

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Machines : SendRequest(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : DeliverAdmit(m)
    \/ \E m \in Machines : DeliverReject(m)
    \/ ProcessQueue
    \/ \E m \in Machines : RefillCredit(m)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

QueueWithinCapacity == Len(queue) <= Capacity

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Machines = {m1, m2, m3}
    Capacity = 2
    MaxCredit = 2
    MaxRefills = 2
INVARIANT QueueWithinCapacity
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A regional vending-machine network reports restock needs to a single central depot. Each machine may send a restock request over an unreliable network path to the depot; because the network can reorder messages, requests from different machines (and even successive deliveries) can arrive at the depot in a different order than they were sent, and there is no way for the depot to tell how stale any given request is. The depot itself maintains a bounded work queue of admitted restock jobs waiting to be serviced, and protects that bound with backpressure: machines are only allowed to send while they hold local sending credit, and even a delivered request is only admitted into the queue if the queue currently has room, otherwise the depot drops it rather than let the queue grow past its bound. Because credit is granted to machines out of a small shared refill budget (so the depot cannot promise unlimited retries) and because delivery order is not guaranteed, a machine's belief about how much room the depot has can be stale by the time its request actually arrives — the depot's own admission check at delivery time is therefore the only thing that must never be violated, not the machines' credit bookkeeping.

The full action set is: (1) SendRequest — a machine holding at least one unit of local credit and with no request currently in flight spends one unit of credit and puts a restock request into the network (an unordered, reorder-prone medium modeled as a set of undelivered requests); (2) DeliverAdmit — the network delivers a machine's in-flight request to the depot, and because the queue currently has room the depot appends the job to its bounded work queue; (3) DeliverReject — the network delivers a machine's in-flight request, but the queue is currently completely full, so the depot drops the request instead of admitting it, enforcing backpressure at the point of delivery; (4) ProcessQueue — the depot's worker removes the oldest admitted job from the front of the queue to service it; (5) RefillCredit — while the shared refill budget still has units left, the depot grants one more unit of sending credit back to a machine that is below its per-machine cap, letting it send again later.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of jobs currently held in the depot's bounded work queue never exceeds the queue's fixed capacity.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od14m3p2t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A wildfire drone swarm elects a leader that assigns grid sectors from a
\* shared pool to active surveillance and later archives them once a fire
\* is out. The leader can crash silently, triggering failover to a new
\* leader. A privileged ground-control admin can also move sectors between
\* the pool and the other two states at any time, regardless of leader
\* state. The invariant protects the conservation law: sectors only ever
\* move between pool/assigned/archived, never created or destroyed.

CONSTANTS Drones, InitLeader, NoneD, TotalSectors

VARIABLES leader, term, crashedLeader, pool, assigned, archived

TypeOK ==
    /\ leader \in Drones
    /\ term \in Nat
    /\ crashedLeader \in Drones \cup {NoneD}
    /\ pool \in 0..TotalSectors
    /\ assigned \in 0..TotalSectors
    /\ archived \in 0..TotalSectors

Init ==
    /\ leader = InitLeader
    /\ term = 0
    /\ crashedLeader = NoneD
    /\ pool = TotalSectors
    /\ assigned = 0
    /\ archived = 0

\* The current leader crashes silently and stops leading.
CrashLeader ==
    /\ crashedLeader = NoneD
    /\ crashedLeader' = leader
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, pool, assigned, archived>>

\* A different, still-live drone takes over leadership after a crash.
Failover ==
    /\ leader = crashedLeader
    /\ \E d \in Drones \ {crashedLeader} :
        /\ leader' = d
        /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashedLeader, pool, assigned, archived>>

\* The live leader assigns one pooled sector to active surveillance.
AssignSector ==
    /\ leader # crashedLeader
    /\ pool > 0
    /\ pool' = pool - 1
    /\ assigned' = assigned + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader, archived>>

\* The live leader archives one actively-surveilled sector as confirmed-out.
ArchiveSector ==
    /\ leader # crashedLeader
    /\ assigned > 0
    /\ assigned' = assigned - 1
    /\ archived' = archived + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader, pool>>

\* Ground control reclaims an assigned sector back to the pool, regardless
\* of leader state, for emergency redirection of coverage.
AdminReclaim ==
    /\ assigned > 0
    /\ assigned' = assigned - 1
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader, archived>>

\* Ground control restores an archived sector to the pool if a fire
\* reignites, regardless of leader state.
AdminRestore ==
    /\ archived > 0
    /\ archived' = archived - 1
    /\ pool' = pool + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader, assigned>>

Next ==
    \/ CrashLeader
    \/ Failover
    \/ AssignSector
    \/ ArchiveSector
    \/ AdminReclaim
    \/ AdminRestore

vars == <<leader, term, crashedLeader, pool, assigned, archived>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: no sector is ever created or destroyed by any leader or admin
\* action -- it only ever moves between pool, assigned, and archived.
SectorsConserved == pool + assigned + archived = TotalSectors

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Drones = {d1, d2, d3}
    InitLeader = d1
    NoneD = noned
    TotalSectors = 3
INVARIANT SectorsConserved
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A swarm of wildfire surveillance drones monitors a fixed number of forest grid sectors during an active wildfire response. At any time exactly one drone in the swarm is the elected leader, responsible for assigning sectors out of a shared unassigned pool to active surveillance duty, and for archiving a sector once its fire has been confirmed extinguished. Every sector is, at all times, in exactly one of three states: waiting in the unassigned pool, actively assigned to a drone for surveillance, or archived as confirmed-out -- and the total count across all three never changes, since sectors are only ever moved between these three states, never created or destroyed. The elected leader drone can crash silently at any time; when it does, the swarm eventually elects a new leader from the remaining drones and bumps the leadership term, and sector assignment resumes once a live leader is in place. In addition, a privileged ground-control admin can intervene at any time, independent of who the current leader is or whether the leader has crashed: the admin may reclaim an actively-assigned sector back into the unassigned pool (for emergency redirection of coverage) or restore an archived sector back into the unassigned pool (if a fire reignites) -- but every admin action, like every leader action, only ever moves a sector between the three states and never creates or destroys one.

The system's actions are: (1) CrashLeader -- the current leader drone crashes silently and stops acting as leader; (2) Failover -- once the leader has crashed, the swarm elects a different, still-live drone as the new leader and increments the leadership term; (3) AssignSector -- the live (non-crashed) leader takes one sector from the unassigned pool and marks it actively assigned for surveillance; (4) ArchiveSector -- the live leader marks one actively-assigned sector as archived (its fire confirmed extinguished); (5) AdminReclaim -- the ground-control admin moves one actively-assigned sector back into the unassigned pool, regardless of leader state; (6) AdminRestore -- the ground-control admin moves one archived sector back into the unassigned pool, regardless of leader state.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of sectors waiting in the unassigned pool, plus the number actively assigned to surveillance, plus the number archived as confirmed-out, equals the fixed total number of sectors the swarm started with -- no sector is ever created or destroyed by any leader action or any admin override.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od15m4p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Workers, QueueCap, MaxQueueCap

\* Workers are member firms; the intake queue is an unordered pool (not a
\* sequence) because the gateway can reorder arrivals, so Admit may pull any
\* pending request next regardless of submission order. MutualExclusion
\* protects the single-slot auction engine: holders never grows past size 1.
\* cap is the queue's live capacity: it only ever grows (bounded by
\* MaxQueueCap), so raising it can loosen Submit/Reject but never blocks or
\* reverses progress already made toward admitting and serving a firm.
VARIABLES waiting, pending, rejected, holders, served, cap

TypeOK == waiting \subseteq Workers /\ pending \subseteq Workers
          /\ rejected \subseteq Workers /\ holders \subseteq Workers
          /\ served \subseteq Workers /\ cap \in QueueCap..MaxQueueCap

Init == waiting = Workers /\ pending = {} /\ rejected = {}
        /\ holders = {} /\ served = {} /\ cap = QueueCap

\* Named once so every admission guard below measures queue fullness the
\* same way against the current live capacity.
PendingCount == Cardinality(pending)

\* A waiting firm enters the bounded queue if there is room under the
\* current live capacity.
Submit(w) == w \in waiting /\ PendingCount < cap
             /\ waiting' = waiting \ {w} /\ pending' = pending \cup {w}
             /\ UNCHANGED <<rejected, holders, served, cap>>

\* Backpressure: a waiting firm arriving while the queue is full is dropped.
Reject(w) == w \in waiting /\ PendingCount = cap
             /\ waiting' = waiting \ {w} /\ rejected' = rejected \cup {w}
             /\ UNCHANGED <<pending, holders, served, cap>>

\* A rejected firm resubmits once the queue has room again.
Retry(w) == w \in rejected /\ PendingCount < cap
            /\ rejected' = rejected \ {w} /\ pending' = pending \cup {w}
            /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, holders, served, cap>>

\* Reordering: any pending request, not necessarily the oldest, may be
\* pulled into the single engine slot once it is free.
Admit == holders = {} /\ pending # {}
         /\ \E w \in pending: pending' = pending \ {w} /\ holders' = {w}
         /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, rejected, served, cap>>

Release == holders # {}
           /\ served' = served \cup holders /\ holders' = {}
           /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, pending, rejected, cap>>

\* Operations raises the intake queue's live capacity by one, up to a fixed
\* ceiling, modeling the exchange provisioning more gateway throughput
\* mid-session. Monotonic and bounded, so it can only ever relax the
\* Submit/Reject/Retry guards, never take capacity away or stall anything.
Expand == cap < MaxQueueCap /\ cap' = cap + 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, pending, rejected, holders, served>>

\* Operations may also shrink live capacity back down under load-shedding,
\* never below the original QueueCap floor. Existing pending/holders/served
\* members are untouched -- only future Submit/Retry admissions get
\* tighter -- and Retry already carries strong fairness (SF), so a firm
\* that keeps becoming retry-eligible infinitely often is still guaranteed
\* to eventually get back in, even if capacity flaps up and down meanwhile.
Shrink == cap > QueueCap /\ cap' = cap - 1
          /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, pending, rejected, holders, served>>

\* Combinator used only for fairness: whichever of Submit/Reject applies to a
\* given firm, it must not stall forever while that firm is still waiting.
LeaveWaiting(w) == Submit(w) \/ Reject(w)

Next == (\E w \in Workers: Submit(w)) \/ (\E w \in Workers: Reject(w))
        \/ (\E w \in Workers: Retry(w)) \/ Admit \/ Release \/ Expand \/ Shrink

vars == <<waiting, pending, rejected, holders, served, cap>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ (\A w \in Workers: WF_vars(LeaveWaiting(w)))
        /\ (\A w \in Workers: SF_vars(Retry(w)))
        /\ WF_vars(Admit) /\ WF_vars(Release)

\* SAFETY: the auction engine is a single critical resource.
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(holders) <= 1

\* LIVENESS: every firm's request is eventually folded into the price.
AllWorkersServed == <>(served = Workers)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {w1, w2, w3}
    QueueCap = 2
    MaxQueueCap = 3
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY AllWorkersServed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A regional stock exchange runs a single-threaded opening-auction price-discovery
engine. Before the opening bell, member firms submit indicative order requests
that must each be fed, one at a time, into the auction engine so it can fold
that firm's interest into the running opening-price calculation. Because the
exchange's inbound gateway can reorder packets under load, requests do not
arrive at the engine's intake queue in the order the firms sent them -- the
intake queue is modeled as an unordered pool of pending requests rather than a
FIFO, so any pending request can be the next one pulled into the engine
regardless of when it was submitted.

The intake queue is a bounded work queue with backpressure: it can hold at
most the queue's current live capacity worth of pending requests at once,
starting at QueueCap. A firm whose request arrives while the queue is full is
not queued at all -- it is immediately rejected (backpressure signal) and
must resubmit later once the queue has drained enough to accept it again (a
retry). The auction engine itself is a single critical resource: at most one
firm's request may be "in the engine" being folded into the price
calculation at any moment, and while an engine slot is occupied no other
firm's request may be pulled in. Separately, exchange operations can raise
the intake queue's live capacity mid-session (for example by provisioning
more gateway throughput before a busy open), one unit at a time up to a
fixed ceiling MaxQueueCap; this capacity only ever grows, so it can loosen
backpressure but never suddenly reject a request that was already accepted.

The full action set is:
  - Submit(w): a waiting firm w hands its request to the intake queue, which
    succeeds only if the queue currently has room under its current live
    capacity.
  - Reject(w): a waiting firm w's request arrives while the queue is full
    (at its current live capacity), so it is dropped by backpressure and
    marked rejected instead of queued.
  - Retry(w): a previously rejected firm w resubmits its request, which
    succeeds only if the queue currently has room under its current live
    capacity.
  - Admit: whenever the engine is free and the intake queue is non-empty, one
    pending request is pulled from the pool nondeterministically (reflecting
    that reordering means arrival order is not preserved) and occupies the
    sole engine slot.
  - Release: the firm currently occupying the engine slot finishes being
    folded into the opening price and is marked served, freeing the slot.
  - Expand: exchange operations raise the intake queue's live capacity by
    one, provided it has not yet reached the fixed ceiling MaxQueueCap.
  - Shrink: exchange operations lower the intake queue's live capacity by
    one under load-shedding, provided it has not yet fallen back to the
    original QueueCap floor; firms already pending, in the engine, or
    served are unaffected -- only future Submit/Retry admissions face the
    tighter limit.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one firm's request occupies
the auction engine's single processing slot at a time.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every member firm that starts out waiting to submit its
opening-auction request is eventually served by the engine, even though its
first attempt may be bounced by backpressure and its request may be pulled
into the engine out of submission order due to reordering.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m2p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A pharmacy dispensing arm is granted to a terminal only after a two-phase
\* commit round with two guarding participants (controller, ledger). Only
\* one round, and one arm holder, exist at a time -- that serialization is
\* what the safety invariant protects. One participant may crash silently
\* mid-round after voting; because it can never vote again, every later
\* round would wait on it forever, so a timeout permanently excuses it and
\* aborts the stuck round, letting future rounds route around it.
CONSTANTS Terminals, Participants, NoneT, NoneP

VARIABLES coordinator, votes, armHolders, crashed, excused, done

Init ==
    /\ coordinator = NoneT
    /\ votes = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ armHolders = {}
    /\ crashed = NoneP
    /\ excused = {}
    /\ done = {}

\* A terminal starts a fresh round: no round in flight, arm free.
StartRound(t) ==
    /\ coordinator = NoneT
    /\ armHolders = {}
    /\ coordinator' = t
    /\ votes' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<armHolders, crashed, excused, done>>

\* A healthy participant that has not yet voted this round votes yes.
Vote(p) ==
    /\ coordinator # NoneT
    /\ votes[p] = "none"
    /\ p # crashed
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![p] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, armHolders, crashed, excused, done>>

\* A participant silently crashes, but only after already voting yes this round.
Crash ==
    /\ crashed = NoneP
    /\ coordinator # NoneT
    /\ \E p \in Participants:
         /\ votes[p] = "yes"
         /\ crashed' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, votes, armHolders, excused, done>>

\* Once every participant has voted yes or been excused, and the arm is
\* free, the coordinator commits and the terminal is granted the arm.
Commit ==
    /\ coordinator # NoneT
    /\ armHolders = {}
    /\ \A p \in Participants: p \in excused \/ votes[p] = "yes"
    /\ armHolders' = {coordinator}
    /\ coordinator' = NoneT
    /\ votes' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, excused, done>>

\* The terminal holding the arm finishes dispensing and releases the arm.
Finish(t) ==
    /\ t \in armHolders
    /\ armHolders' = armHolders \ {t}
    /\ done' = done \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coordinator, votes, crashed, excused>>

\* Timeout: a round is in flight and stuck waiting on the already-crashed
\* participant's vote; excuse it permanently and abort the stuck round.
Timeout ==
    /\ crashed # NoneP
    /\ crashed \notin excused
    /\ coordinator # NoneT
    /\ votes[crashed] = "none"
    /\ excused' = excused \cup {crashed}
    /\ coordinator' = NoneT
    /\ votes' = [p \in Participants |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<armHolders, crashed, done>>

Next ==
    \/ (\E t \in Terminals: StartRound(t))
    \/ (\E p \in Participants: Vote(p))
    \/ Crash
    \/ Commit
    \/ (\E t \in Terminals: Finish(t))
    \/ Timeout

vars == <<coordinator, votes, armHolders, crashed, excused, done>>

\* StartRound(t) is only intermittently enabled -- other terminals can keep
\* winning the free round slot forever -- so it needs strong fairness (SF),
\* not weak fairness, to guarantee every terminal eventually gets a turn.
Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ (\A t \in Terminals: SF_vars(StartRound(t)))
    /\ (\A p \in Participants: WF_vars(Vote(p)))
    /\ WF_vars(Commit)
    /\ WF_vars(Timeout)
    /\ (\A t \in Terminals: SF_vars(Finish(t)))

\* Mutual exclusion of the dispensing arm: never more than one holder.
ArmMutex == Cardinality(armHolders) <= 1

\* Every terminal that ever starts a round eventually finishes dispensing,
\* despite a mid-round silent crash and the resulting permanent excuse.
AllTerminalsServed == \A t \in Terminals: <>(t \in done)
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Terminals = {t1, t2, t3}
    Participants = {ctrl, ledger}
    NoneT = nonet
    NoneP = nonep
INVARIANT ArmMutex
PROPERTY AllTerminalsServed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A hospital pharmacy runs an automated dispensing cabinet shared by several nursing-station terminals. The cabinet has exactly one mechanical dispensing arm -- the critical resource -- and only one terminal's prescription-fill request may drive the arm at a time. Before a terminal is allowed to drive the arm, it runs a two-phase commit round against two guarding participants (a controller process and an inventory-ledger process). Only one round can be in flight at a time. In phase one (prepare), the coordinating terminal starts the round and both participants are asked to vote; each healthy participant votes yes for that round, locking its own local state. In phase two, once every participant has either voted yes for the round or has previously been formally excused (see below), the coordinator commits: the requesting terminal is granted the dispensing arm. The twist is that either one of the two guarding participants can crash silently at any point while a round is in flight, after having already cast its yes vote for that round; a crashed participant never votes again, in that round or any future one. Because a crashed participant can never vote again, every round started after the crash would wait forever for its vote -- so a timeout mechanism watches for exactly this: if a round is in flight and is waiting on a vote from the (already) crashed participant, the timeout fires, formally excuses that participant once and for all (its vote requirement is waived for every future round from then on), and aborts the current round so a fresh one can start. The system's six actions are: (1) a terminal starts a fresh two-phase commit round, provided no round is currently in flight and no one currently holds the dispensing arm, (2) a participant that has not crashed and has not yet voted in the current round votes yes, (3) one of the two participants silently crashes, but only after it has already cast a yes vote in the round that is in flight, (4) once every participant has either voted yes in the current round or been excused, and the dispensing arm is currently free, the coordinator commits the round and grants the requesting terminal the dispensing arm, ending the round, (5) the terminal currently holding the dispensing arm finishes dispensing, releases the arm, and is marked as having been served, and (6) if a round is in flight and stuck waiting on a vote from the already-crashed participant, the timeout fires: that participant is excused permanently and the stuck round is aborted, freeing the round slot for a new one. SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, the dispensing arm is held by at most one terminal. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every terminal that starts a two-phase commit round eventually finishes dispensing and holds (then releases) the arm, even though one of the two guarding participants may crash silently mid-round and every round after that must route around its permanently missing vote via the timeout's excuse mechanism.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od16m8p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Pharmacists, Cabinets, SlotsPerCabinet, NoneP

\* Slots are (cabinet, index) pairs so CabinetOf is derivable, not stored.
\* Two-level locking: a coarse cabinetLock must be held before the matching
\* fine slotLock, and only the fine-lock holder may commit allocatedTo. A
\* silent Crash freezes locks; Recover reclaims locks but never touches an
\* already-committed allocation, which is exactly what NoDoubleAllocation
\* below relies on to stay true across a crash.
Slots == Cabinets \X (1..SlotsPerCabinet)
CabinetOf(s) == s[1]

VARIABLES cabinetLock, slotLock, allocatedTo, crashed

TypeOK == cabinetLock \in [Cabinets -> Pharmacists \cup {NoneP}]
          /\ slotLock \in [Slots -> Pharmacists \cup {NoneP}]
          /\ allocatedTo \in [Slots -> Pharmacists \cup {NoneP}]
          /\ crashed \in Pharmacists \cup {NoneP}

Init == cabinetLock = [c \in Cabinets |-> NoneP]
        /\ slotLock = [s \in Slots |-> NoneP]
        /\ allocatedTo = [s \in Slots |-> NoneP]
        /\ crashed = NoneP

AcquireCabinet(p, c) == p # crashed /\ cabinetLock[c] = NoneP
                        /\ (\A c2 \in Cabinets: cabinetLock[c2] # p)
                        /\ cabinetLock' = [cabinetLock EXCEPT ![c] = p]
                        /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, allocatedTo, crashed>>

AcquireSlot(p, s) == p # crashed /\ cabinetLock[CabinetOf(s)] = p
                     /\ slotLock[s] = NoneP /\ allocatedTo[s] = NoneP
                     /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = p]
                     /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, allocatedTo, crashed>>

Allocate(p, s) == p # crashed /\ slotLock[s] = p /\ allocatedTo[s] = NoneP
                  /\ allocatedTo' = [allocatedTo EXCEPT ![s] = p]
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, slotLock, crashed>>

Dispense(p, s) == p # crashed /\ slotLock[s] = p /\ allocatedTo[s] = p
                  /\ allocatedTo' = [allocatedTo EXCEPT ![s] = NoneP]
                  /\ slotLock' = [slotLock EXCEPT ![s] = NoneP]
                  /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, crashed>>

ReleaseCabinet(p, c) == p # crashed /\ cabinetLock[c] = p
                        /\ (\A s \in Slots: CabinetOf(s) = c => slotLock[s] # p)
                        /\ cabinetLock' = [cabinetLock EXCEPT ![c] = NoneP]
                        /\ UNCHANGED <<slotLock, allocatedTo, crashed>>

\* Exactly one workstation, ever, may crash silently.
Crash(p) == crashed = NoneP /\ crashed' = p
            /\ UNCHANGED <<cabinetLock, slotLock, allocatedTo>>

\* Recovery reclaims locks only -- committed allocations are untouched.
Recover(p) == crashed = p
              /\ slotLock' = [s \in Slots |-> IF slotLock[s] = p THEN NoneP ELSE slotLock[s]]
              /\ cabinetLock' = [c \in Cabinets |-> IF cabinetLock[c] = p THEN NoneP ELSE cabinetLock[c]]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<allocatedTo, crashed>>

Next == (\E p \in Pharmacists, c \in Cabinets: AcquireCabinet(p, c))
        \/ (\E p \in Pharmacists, s \in Slots: AcquireSlot(p, s))
        \/ (\E p \in Pharmacists, s \in Slots: Allocate(p, s))
        \/ (\E p \in Pharmacists, s \in Slots: Dispense(p, s))
        \/ (\E p \in Pharmacists, c \in Cabinets: ReleaseCabinet(p, c))
        \/ (\E p \in Pharmacists: Crash(p))
        \/ (\E p \in Pharmacists: Recover(p))

vars == <<cabinetLock, slotLock, allocatedTo, crashed>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No double allocation: a committed allocation's owner is the only
\* workstation ever allowed to co-hold that slot's fine lock.
NoDoubleAllocation == \A s \in Slots:
    allocatedTo[s] # NoneP => slotLock[s] \in {NoneP, allocatedTo[s]}
====
cfg_text:
SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Pharmacists = {p1, p2, p3}
    Cabinets = {c1, c2}
    SlotsPerCabinet = 2
    NoneP = none
INVARIANT NoDoubleAllocation
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A hospital pharmacy has several automated dispensing cabinets, each holding a
fixed number of physical dispensing slots that a filled prescription can
occupy while it waits for pickup. Several pharmacist workstations may be
filling prescriptions at the same time, so access to slots is protected by a
two-level (hierarchical) locking discipline: a pharmacist must first acquire
the coarse lock on an entire cabinet before it may touch any slot inside that
cabinet, and only after holding the cabinet's coarse lock may it acquire the
fine-grained lock on one specific slot within that cabinet. A slot's contents
(the fact that a particular prescription now occupies it) are only committed
once the pharmacist, holding the slot's fine lock, explicitly allocates the
slot; simply holding the fine lock does not yet commit an allocation.

The twist is that a pharmacist workstation can crash silently at any time,
possibly while it still holds a coarse cabinet lock and/or a fine slot lock.
A crashed workstation does nothing further, but the system runs a recovery
step that reclaims any coarse and fine locks still held by the crashed
workstation so other workstations are not blocked forever. Recovery only
releases locks -- it never touches (creates or erases) a slot's committed
allocation record, so a slot the crashed workstation had already fully
allocated before crashing remains allocated to it, while a slot it had merely
locked but not yet allocated becomes free again for another workstation to
claim.

The full action set is:
  - AcquireCabinet(p, c): workstation p, not crashed and not already holding
    any cabinet's coarse lock, takes the free coarse lock on cabinet c.
  - AcquireSlot(p, s): workstation p, holding the coarse lock on the cabinet
    that owns slot s, takes the free fine lock on s provided s currently has
    no committed allocation.
  - Allocate(p, s): workstation p, holding the fine lock on unallocated slot
    s, commits the allocation of s to itself (the prescription now occupies
    the slot).
  - Dispense(p, s): workstation p, holding the fine lock on a slot s it has
    allocated, completes the pickup, clearing both the allocation record and
    the fine lock so the slot becomes available again.
  - ReleaseCabinet(p, c): workstation p, holding the coarse lock on cabinet
    c and holding no fine lock on any slot inside c, releases the coarse
    lock.
  - Crash(p): at most one workstation, chosen nondeterministically, crashes
    silently at any point, freezing its locks exactly as they were.
  - Recover(p): once workstation p has crashed, the recovery step clears
    every coarse and fine lock still held by p, leaving any already-
    committed allocation records made by p untouched.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every slot, if the slot has a committed allocation
record naming some workstation, then the slot's fine lock, whenever it is
held at all, is held by that very same workstation -- no other workstation's
lock can coexist with someone else's committed allocation of the same slot,
even across a silent crash and recovery.

---- MODULE W4Od17m0p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Handlers, Bags, NoBag, RescanBudget

\* Optimistic locking with retry: a handler snapshots a bag slot's version,
\* then CAS-loads only if the version has not moved; otherwise it retries.
\* AtMostOnceLoad protects the fact that the irreversible load can never
\* fire twice for the same bag, no matter how retries or a silent crash
\* interleave with a bounded number of adversarial slot revisions.
VARIABLES version, loadCount, assigned, readVer, crashed, rescansLeft

vars == <<version, loadCount, assigned, readVer, crashed, rescansLeft>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in [Bags -> Nat]
    /\ loadCount \in [Bags -> 0..1]
    /\ assigned \in [Handlers -> Bags \cup {NoBag}]
    /\ readVer \in [Handlers -> Nat]
    /\ crashed \subseteq Handlers
    /\ rescansLeft \in 0..RescanBudget

Init ==
    /\ version = [b \in Bags |-> 0]
    /\ loadCount = [b \in Bags |-> 0]
    /\ assigned = [h \in Handlers |-> NoBag]
    /\ readVer = [h \in Handlers |-> 0]
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ rescansLeft = RescanBudget

\* An idle, non-crashed handler snapshots an unloaded bag's slot version.
StartAttemptHB(h, b) ==
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ assigned[h] = NoBag
    /\ loadCount[b] = 0
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![h] = b]
    /\ readVer' = [readVer EXCEPT ![h] = version[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, loadCount, crashed, rescansLeft>>

\* CAS succeeds: the snapshot still matches, so the irreversible load fires.
LoadSuccessH(h) ==
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ assigned[h] # NoBag
    /\ LET b == assigned[h] IN
        /\ loadCount[b] = 0
        /\ readVer[h] = version[b]
        /\ loadCount' = [loadCount EXCEPT ![b] = 1]
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
        /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![h] = NoBag]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<readVer, crashed, rescansLeft>>

\* CAS fails (slot moved, bag still unloaded): refresh the snapshot and retry later.
RetryH(h) ==
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ assigned[h] # NoBag
    /\ LET b == assigned[h] IN
        /\ loadCount[b] = 0
        /\ readVer[h] # version[b]
        /\ readVer' = [readVer EXCEPT ![h] = version[b]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, loadCount, assigned, crashed, rescansLeft>>

\* Another handler already finished this bag; give up and go idle.
AbandonH(h) ==
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ assigned[h] # NoBag
    /\ loadCount[assigned[h]] = 1
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![h] = NoBag]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, loadCount, readVer, crashed, rescansLeft>>

\* Bounded adversarial interference: the manifest system revises a still
\* unloaded slot, invalidating any outstanding snapshot for it.
RescanSlot(b) ==
    /\ rescansLeft > 0
    /\ loadCount[b] = 0
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ rescansLeft' = rescansLeft - 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<loadCount, assigned, readVer, crashed>>

\* Twist: at most one handler ever silently crashes and stops acting.
CrashH(h) ==
    /\ h \notin crashed
    /\ Cardinality(crashed) = 0
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, loadCount, assigned, readVer, rescansLeft>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers, b \in Bags : StartAttemptHB(h, b)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : LoadSuccessH(h)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : RetryH(h)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : AbandonH(h)
    \/ \E b \in Bags : RescanSlot(b)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : CrashH(h)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Handlers, b \in Bags : StartAttemptHB(h, b))
    /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Handlers : LoadSuccessH(h))
    /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Handlers : RetryH(h))
    /\ WF_vars(\E h \in Handlers : AbandonH(h))

AtMostOnceLoad == \A b \in Bags : loadCount[b] <= 1

AllBagsEventuallyLoaded == <>(\A b \in Bags : loadCount[b] = 1)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Handlers = {h1, h2}
    Bags = {bg1, bg2}
    NoBag = nobag
    RescanBudget = 1
INVARIANT AtMostOnceLoad
PROPERTY AllBagsEventuallyLoaded
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An airport baggage router moves bags toward the loading bay for their assigned flight. Each bag has a manifest slot with a version counter, and loading a bag onto its flight is irreversible: once done it cannot be undone or repeated. Handlers process bags using optimistic locking with retry instead of exclusive locks: a handler snapshots a bag's current slot version, does other work, and then attempts a compare-and-swap against that snapshot; if the slot's version has not moved, the compare-and-swap succeeds and the load happens; if it has moved, the handler must refresh its snapshot and try again.

Concretely, the full action set is: (1) StartAttempt — an idle handler picks a bag that has not yet been loaded and snapshots that bag's current slot version, becoming busy on it; (2) LoadSuccess — a busy handler whose snapshot still matches the bag's current slot version performs the irreversible load: the bag's load count moves from 0 to 1, the slot version is bumped, and the handler becomes idle again; (3) RetryAfterConflict — a busy handler whose snapshot no longer matches the bag's current slot version, and whose bag is still not loaded, refreshes its snapshot to the current version so it can attempt again later; (4) AbandonCompleted — a busy handler discovers that the bag it was working on has already been loaded by someone else in the meantime, and gives up on it, becoming idle; (5) RescanSlot — the router's manifest system may, a strictly limited number of times overall, revise a not-yet-loaded bag's slot (for example, a late gate reassignment), bumping its version and invalidating any handler's outstanding snapshot for that bag, which forces a later retry; (6) CrashHandler — the twist: at most one handler, at any point, may silently crash and permanently stop taking any further action, abandoning whatever it was doing without releasing any exclusive resource (there is none, since locking here is optimistic), so other handlers are never blocked by it.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every bag, the irreversible load action fires at most once — a bag's load count never exceeds 1.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every bag is eventually loaded exactly once, even though at most one handler may silently crash mid-attempt and the router's manifest system may inject a bounded number of slot revisions that force retries, because the surviving handlers keep retrying with optimistic locking until each bag's compare-and-swap succeeds.

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* Smart-home door-lock controllers share one access-policy record (version + owner).
\* A controller updates it via compare-and-swap: the write only lands if the
\* controller's locally observed version still matches the shared version.
\* An admin console can force-write the record at any time, bypassing CAS.
\* The invariant protects against a "lost update": a controller must never
\* believe (via matching version numbers) that it is synced with the shared
\* record while actually holding a stale owner value.
CONSTANTS Controllers, Admin, InitOwner, MaxVersion

VARIABLES version, owner, obsVersion, obsOwner

TypeOK ==
    /\ version \in 0..MaxVersion
    /\ owner \in Controllers \cup {Admin}
    /\ obsVersion \in [Controllers -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ obsOwner \in [Controllers -> Controllers \cup {Admin}]

Init ==
    /\ version = 0
    /\ owner = InitOwner
    /\ obsVersion = [c \in Controllers |-> 0]
    /\ obsOwner = [c \in Controllers |-> InitOwner]

\* A controller re-reads the shared record into its local cache.
Refresh(c) ==
    /\ obsVersion' = [obsVersion EXCEPT ![c] = version]
    /\ obsOwner' = [obsOwner EXCEPT ![c] = owner]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner>>

\* A controller's compare-and-swap write lands because its observed version
\* still matches the shared version; the shared record advances and the
\* controller's own cache is updated to the post-write value atomically.
CASSucceed(c) ==
    /\ obsVersion[c] = version
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ owner' = c
    /\ obsVersion' = [obsVersion EXCEPT ![c] = version + 1]
    /\ obsOwner' = [obsOwner EXCEPT ![c] = c]

\* A controller's compare-and-swap attempt is rejected because some other
\* write already advanced the shared version; the record is left untouched
\* and the controller must Refresh separately before trying again.
CASFail(c) ==
    /\ obsVersion[c] # version
    /\ UNCHANGED <<version, owner, obsVersion, obsOwner>>

\* The privileged admin console force-writes the record unconditionally,
\* bypassing the CAS check; no controller's cache is updated by this.
AdminOverride ==
    /\ version < MaxVersion
    /\ version' = version + 1
    /\ owner' = Admin
    /\ UNCHANGED <<obsVersion, obsOwner>>

Next ==
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: Refresh(c))
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: CASSucceed(c))
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: CASFail(c))
    \/ AdminOverride

vars == <<version, owner, obsVersion, obsOwner>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: any controller whose observed version matches the
\* shared record's current version must also agree on who the owner is.
NoLostUpdates == \A c \in Controllers: obsVersion[c] = version => obsOwner[c] = owner
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
    Admin = admin
    InitOwner = c1
    MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A smart-home vendor operates a network of door-lock controllers that all share one authoritative access-policy record for the front door (the record holds a policy version number and the name of the resident who last set it). Each controller keeps a locally cached copy of the record's version. To change the policy (e.g. add or revoke a guest code), a controller reads the shared record, computes a new value, and then writes it back using a compare-and-swap: the write only succeeds if the version the controller last observed still matches the shared record's current version, and on success the shared version is bumped by one and the record's owner field is set to the writing controller. If another controller's write intervened between the read and the write attempt, the compare-and-swap fails and the record is left untouched, forcing the controller to retry from a fresh read. Separately, a privileged home-admin console can perform an admin override at any time: it force-writes the shared record directly, bypassing the compare-and-swap check entirely, bumping the version and setting itself as owner regardless of what any controller last observed. Whenever a controller successfully performs a normal compare-and-swap write or refreshes its local cache by re-reading the shared record, its local observed version is updated to match the shared record's version at that instant. The system's four actions are: (1) a controller reads/refreshes its locally observed version from the shared record, (2) a controller attempts a compare-and-swap write using its locally observed version, which succeeds only if that version still equals the shared version, (3) a controller's compare-and-swap write fails silently (version mismatch) and leaves the shared record unchanged, and (4) the admin console force-overrides the shared record unconditionally. SAFETY PROPERTY: whenever a controller's locally observed version equals the shared record's current version, that controller must also agree with the shared record on who the current owner is -- i.e. no controller ever believes it is looking at the current record while actually holding a stale owner value (no update, whether from a normal compare-and-swap or an admin override, is ever silently lost from the perspective of a controller that thinks it is up to date).

---- MODULE W4Od18m7p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A smart-home hub shares a capacity-bounded pool of unlock credentials
\* among door locks via a compare-and-swap claim/release register. The
\* homeowner may change the declared capacity at runtime, minting or
\* reclaiming credentials. The invariant protects the conservation law:
\* available + held always equals the current capacity, since claims and
\* releases only move credentials and only capacity changes mint/reclaim
\* them.

CONSTANTS Locks, InitCapacity, MaxCapacity, MaxDelta

VARIABLES capacity, available, heldBy, waiting

TypeOK ==
    /\ capacity \in 0..MaxCapacity
    /\ available \in 0..MaxCapacity
    /\ heldBy \subseteq Locks
    /\ waiting \subseteq Locks

Init ==
    /\ capacity = InitCapacity
    /\ available = InitCapacity
    /\ heldBy = {}
    /\ waiting = {}

\* A lock with no pending request and no held credential asks for one.
RequestCredential(l) ==
    /\ l \notin waiting
    /\ l \notin heldBy
    /\ waiting' = waiting \cup {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, available, heldBy>>

\* A waiting lock atomically claims a credential via compare-and-swap,
\* provided the pool is currently non-empty.
ClaimCredential(l) ==
    /\ l \in waiting
    /\ available > 0
    /\ available' = available - 1
    /\ heldBy' = heldBy \cup {l}
    /\ waiting' = waiting \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED capacity

\* A holding lock returns its credential to the pool.
ReleaseCredential(l) ==
    /\ l \in heldBy
    /\ heldBy' = heldBy \ {l}
    /\ available' = available + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<capacity, waiting>>

\* The homeowner raises capacity, minting new credentials into the pool.
IncreaseCapacity ==
    /\ \E k \in 1..MaxDelta :
        /\ capacity + k <= MaxCapacity
        /\ capacity' = capacity + k
        /\ available' = available + k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<heldBy, waiting>>

\* The homeowner lowers capacity, reclaiming unclaimed credentials --
\* only when no lock has a pending request, so no request is starved.
DecreaseCapacity ==
    /\ waiting = {}
    /\ \E k \in 1..available :
        /\ capacity' = capacity - k
        /\ available' = available - k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<heldBy, waiting>>

Next ==
    \/ \E l \in Locks : RequestCredential(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : ClaimCredential(l)
    \/ \E l \in Locks : ReleaseCredential(l)
    \/ IncreaseCapacity
    \/ DecreaseCapacity

vars == <<capacity, available, heldBy, waiting>>

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ \A l \in Locks : SF_vars(ClaimCredential(l))
    /\ \A l \in Locks : WF_vars(ReleaseCredential(l))
    /\ WF_vars(IncreaseCapacity)

\* SAFETY: credentials are only ever moved (claim/release) or minted/
\* reclaimed in lockstep with capacity -- never created or destroyed.
CredentialsConserved == available + Cardinality(heldBy) = capacity

\* LIVENESS: every submitted request is eventually granted.
EveryRequestEventuallyGranted ==
    \A l \in Locks : (l \in waiting) ~> (l \in heldBy)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Locks = {front, back, garage}
    InitCapacity = 2
    MaxCapacity = 4
    MaxDelta = 2
INVARIANT CredentialsConserved
PROPERTY EveryRequestEventuallyGranted
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A smart-home hub coordinates a network of smart door locks (front door, back door, garage, gate) that share a limited pool of concurrent unlock credentials, capped by a capacity the hub currently supports. A lock that wants to grant entry must atomically claim one credential from the shared pool via a compare-and-swap register on the hub (it succeeds only if a credential is currently available, decrementing the available count and marking the credential held by that lock); when the lock is done it releases the credential back to the pool. Every credential the hub is tracking is, at all times, either sitting unclaimed in the available pool or currently held by exactly one lock -- and the number of available-plus-held credentials always equals the hub's current declared capacity, since credentials are only ever minted or reclaimed by an explicit capacity change, never silently created or destroyed by a claim or release. The homeowner can change the hub's capacity at runtime: raising it immediately mints that many new credentials into the available pool, while lowering it reclaims that many unclaimed credentials from the available pool (capacity can only be lowered while no lock has a pending, ungranted request, and only by an amount the available pool can actually cover, so a lock's outstanding request is never starved).

The system's actions are: (1) RequestCredential -- a lock that is neither waiting nor currently holding a credential submits a request for one; (2) ClaimCredential -- a waiting lock atomically claims one credential from the pool via compare-and-swap, provided at least one credential is currently available; (3) ReleaseCredential -- a lock currently holding a credential releases it back to the available pool; (4) IncreaseCapacity -- the homeowner raises the hub's capacity by some amount and mints that many new credentials directly into the available pool; (5) DecreaseCapacity -- the homeowner lowers the hub's capacity, reclaiming that many credentials from the available pool, but only when no lock currently has a pending request and only by an amount not exceeding the available pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of credentials sitting unclaimed in the available pool plus the number of credentials currently held by locks equals the hub's current declared capacity -- no credential is ever created or destroyed by a claim, release, or capacity change.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every lock that submits a request for a credential eventually has it granted (moves from waiting to holding), even though the homeowner may repeatedly change the hub's capacity at runtime.

---- MODULE W4Od18m8p0t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* Hierarchical door-lock scheme: a coarse zone lock must be held before the
\* fine-grained actuator lock (which actually drives the deadbolt motor) can
\* be acquired. Releases are two-phase (Send then Deliver) to model an
\* unreliable mesh network that can reorder and delay release messages; the
\* delivery guard is re-checked at delivery time, which is what keeps the
\* mutual-exclusion and coarse-before-fine invariant true even under
\* arbitrary reordering.
CONSTANTS Controllers

VARIABLES zoneHolders, actuatorHolders, zoneRelPending, actRelPending

Init ==
    /\ zoneHolders = {}
    /\ actuatorHolders = {}
    /\ zoneRelPending = {}
    /\ actRelPending = {}

\* A controller acquires the free coarse zone lock outright.
AcquireZone(c) ==
    /\ zoneHolders = {}
    /\ c \notin zoneRelPending
    /\ zoneHolders' = {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<actuatorHolders, zoneRelPending, actRelPending>>

\* A controller holding the zone lock acquires the free fine-grained
\* actuator lock outright.
AcquireActuator(c) ==
    /\ c \in zoneHolders
    /\ actuatorHolders = {}
    /\ actuatorHolders' = {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneHolders, zoneRelPending, actRelPending>>

\* The actuator lock's holder sends a release message; it sits in flight.
SendActuatorRelease(c) ==
    /\ c \in actuatorHolders
    /\ c \notin actRelPending
    /\ actRelPending' = actRelPending \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneHolders, actuatorHolders, zoneRelPending>>

\* A pending actuator-release message is delivered; the guard is re-checked
\* at delivery time, so reordering can only delay, never corrupt, the effect.
DeliverActuatorRelease(c) ==
    /\ c \in actRelPending
    /\ actRelPending' = actRelPending \ {c}
    /\ IF c \in actuatorHolders
       THEN actuatorHolders' = actuatorHolders \ {c}
       ELSE actuatorHolders' = actuatorHolders
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneHolders, zoneRelPending>>

\* The zone lock's holder sends a release message; it sits in flight.
SendZoneRelease(c) ==
    /\ c \in zoneHolders
    /\ c \notin zoneRelPending
    /\ zoneRelPending' = zoneRelPending \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<zoneHolders, actuatorHolders, actRelPending>>

\* A pending zone-release message is delivered only if, at delivery time,
\* the controller still holds the zone lock and no longer holds the
\* actuator lock; otherwise the message stays pending (the reordering
\* hazard the twist describes: an actuator acquisition slipped in first).
DeliverZoneRelease(c) ==
    /\ c \in zoneRelPending
    /\ zoneRelPending' = zoneRelPending \ {c}
    /\ IF c \in zoneHolders /\ c \notin actuatorHolders
       THEN zoneHolders' = zoneHolders \ {c}
       ELSE zoneHolders' = zoneHolders
    /\ UNCHANGED <<actuatorHolders, actRelPending>>

Next ==
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: AcquireZone(c))
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: AcquireActuator(c))
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: SendActuatorRelease(c))
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: DeliverActuatorRelease(c))
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: SendZoneRelease(c))
    \/ (\E c \in Controllers: DeliverZoneRelease(c))

vars == <<zoneHolders, actuatorHolders, zoneRelPending, actRelPending>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Mutual exclusion at both granularities, plus coarse-before-fine coherence:
\* the actuator holder set is always a subset of the zone holder set.
HierarchyOK ==
    /\ Cardinality(zoneHolders) <= 1
    /\ Cardinality(actuatorHolders) <= 1
    /\ actuatorHolders \subseteq zoneHolders
====
