SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Controllers = {c1, c2, c3}
INVARIANT HierarchyOK
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A smart-home vendor's door-lock network protects the physical deadbolt actuator on the front door -- the one critical resource that must never be driven by two lock controllers at the same time. Controllers acquire access to the actuator through a two-level hierarchical locking scheme. First a controller must acquire the single coarse "zone lock" covering the whole front-entry zone (only one controller may hold it at a time). Only after holding the zone lock may a controller acquire the fine-grained "actuator lock" that grants the right to actually drive the deadbolt motor (also held by at most one controller at a time). A controller may only release the zone lock once it no longer holds the actuator lock. The twist is that release messages travel over an unreliable mesh network that can reorder and delay them in transit: releasing a lock is a two-step affair -- a controller first sends a release message, which sits in flight for an arbitrary amount of time before it is finally delivered and actually takes effect, and delivery can happen in any order relative to every other message in flight, including that same controller's other pending messages or a fresh acquisition attempt by another controller. When a release message is finally delivered, the network re-checks, at delivery time (not at send time), whether releasing is still valid; if conditions have changed in the meantime the message simply stays pending until it is safe to apply. The system's six actions are: (1) a controller acquires the zone lock outright, provided no one currently holds it, (2) a controller that holds the zone lock acquires the actuator lock outright, provided no one currently holds it, (3) a controller that currently holds the actuator lock sends a release message for the actuator lock, which then sits pending in the network, (4) a controller's previously sent, still-pending actuator-lock release message is delivered, and provided that controller is still the actuator lock's holder at delivery time, the actuator lock is freed, (5) a controller that currently holds the zone lock sends a release message for the zone lock, which then sits pending in the network, and (6) a controller's previously sent, still-pending zone-lock release message is delivered, and provided that controller is still the zone lock's holder AND no longer holds the actuator lock at delivery time, the zone lock is freed (otherwise the message stays pending, exactly the case where reordering let an actuator-lock acquisition slip in ahead of the zone-lock release taking effect). SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, the zone lock and the actuator lock are each held by at most one controller, and whenever any controller holds the actuator lock that same controller also holds the zone lock (the fine-grained lock is never granted to, nor left held by, a controller that does not also hold the enclosing coarse lock), even though release messages may be arbitrarily reordered and delayed by the mesh network.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od2m3p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Robots, Capacity, InitLeader, NoneR

\* A warehouse robot fleet shares one charging bay with a fixed slot count.
\* Only the current leader may grant docking permission. The leader can
\* crash silently; a failover bumps the term so grants issued under an
\* old term can never be used to dock. The invariant protects the bay's
\* physical slot capacity against ever being oversubscribed.
VARIABLES leader, term, crashedLeader, status, grantTerm

vars == <<leader, term, crashedLeader, status, grantTerm>>

Init == leader = InitLeader
        /\ term = 0
        /\ crashedLeader = NoneR
        /\ status = [r \in Robots |-> "idle"]
        /\ grantTerm = [r \in Robots |-> 0]

Crash == crashedLeader = NoneR
         /\ crashedLeader' = leader
         /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, status, grantTerm>>

Failover == crashedLeader = leader
            /\ \E r \in Robots \ {crashedLeader} :
                 leader' = r /\ term' = term + 1
            /\ UNCHANGED <<crashedLeader, status, grantTerm>>

DockedCount == Cardinality({r \in Robots : status[r] = "docked"})

\* Slots are reserved the moment a grant is issued, not only once a robot
\* physically docks, so ReservedCount (granted + docked) is what must stay
\* under Capacity for GrantDock to remain safe.
ReservedCount == Cardinality({r \in Robots : status[r] \in {"granted", "docked"}})

GrantDock == leader # crashedLeader
             /\ ReservedCount < Capacity
             /\ \E r \in Robots :
                  status[r] = "idle"
                  /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "granted"]
                  /\ grantTerm' = [grantTerm EXCEPT ![r] = term]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader>>

Dock == \E r \in Robots :
           status[r] = "granted"
           /\ grantTerm[r] = term
           /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "docked"]
           /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader, grantTerm>>

Undock == \E r \in Robots :
            status[r] = "docked"
            /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader, grantTerm>>

\* The current leader may revoke an outstanding grant before the robot
\* physically docks -- e.g. the robot missed its docking window or the
\* leader needs the slot for a higher-priority robot -- freeing the
\* reservation that ReservedCount was counting against Capacity.
RevokeGrant == leader # crashedLeader
               /\ \E r \in Robots :
                    status[r] = "granted"
                    /\ status' = [status EXCEPT ![r] = "idle"]
               /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, crashedLeader, grantTerm>>

Next == Crash \/ Failover \/ GrantDock \/ Dock \/ Undock \/ RevokeGrant

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

BayCapacityRespected == DockedCount <= Capacity

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Robots = {r1, r2, r3, r4}
    Capacity = 2
    InitLeader = r1
    NoneR = noner
INVARIANT BayCapacityRespected
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A warehouse operates a small fleet of mobile pick robots that share a single narrow charging bay with a fixed number of power slots. One robot in the fleet is designated the fleet leader, and only the leader is allowed to grant a robot permission to dock at the charging bay (this keeps robots from swarming the bay and jamming it). The leader itself can crash silently at any time -- it simply stops responding, with no warning message to the rest of the fleet. When the current leader has crashed, any other non-crashed robot may notice the silence and hold a failover election, becoming the new leader and bumping the fleet's term counter so stale grants from an old leader are never re-used. Robots move through three states with respect to the bay: idle (not docked, not holding a grant), granted (holds a leader-issued permission to dock but has not yet occupied a slot), and docked (physically occupying one of the bay's power slots). The full action set is: (1) Crash -- the current leader silently fails, recorded in a crashed-leader variable, and no other state changes; (2) Failover -- some non-crashed robot other than the failed leader becomes the new leader and the term counter increments by one, provided the fleet's current leader has in fact crashed; (3) GrantDock -- the current (non-crashed) leader issues a docking grant, tagged with the current term, to one idle robot, moving that robot from idle to granted, provided the number of robots that currently hold a reserved slot (either granted or already docked) is below the bay's fixed slot capacity, since a grant reserves a slot the instant it is issued; (4) Dock -- a robot holding a grant whose term matches the fleet's current term moves from granted to docked, occupying one power slot; (5) Undock -- a docked robot finishes charging and returns to idle, freeing its slot; (6) RevokeGrant -- the current (non-crashed) leader revokes an outstanding grant held by some robot that has not yet docked, for example because the robot missed its docking window or the slot is needed for a higher-priority robot, moving that robot back from granted to idle and freeing the reservation it was holding against the bay's capacity. Grants tagged with an old (pre-failover) term become permanently unusable for docking once a new term begins, because Dock requires the grant's term to equal the current term. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of robots in the docked state never exceeds the charging bay's fixed slot capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od3m3p1t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Coordinators, InitLeader, Updates, MinCapacity, MaxCapacity, InitCapacity

\* Optimistic-concurrency settlement record: baseVersion[u] is the version an
\* instruction read at Prepare time (0 = holding no snapshot); commitVersion[u]
\* is the version it wrote at Commit time (0 = never committed). Commit writes
\* the *stale-checked* snapshot into recordVersion, so if the CAS guard were
\* ever bypassed a superseded write could regress recordVersion below an
\* already-recorded commitVersion -- exactly the lost-update failure
\* NoLostUpdates below is meant to catch. Failover/capacity changes never
\* touch baseVersion or commitVersion, by design.
VARIABLES leader, recordVersion, capacity, baseVersion, commitVersion

TypeOK == leader \in Coordinators /\ recordVersion \in Nat
          /\ capacity \in MinCapacity..MaxCapacity
          /\ baseVersion \in [Updates -> Nat] /\ commitVersion \in [Updates -> Nat]

Init == leader = InitLeader /\ recordVersion = 0 /\ capacity = InitCapacity
        /\ baseVersion = [u \in Updates |-> 0]
        /\ commitVersion = [u \in Updates |-> 0]

\* Snapshot the record's version, bounded by the live capacity.
Prepare(u) == commitVersion[u] = 0 /\ baseVersion[u] = 0
              /\ Cardinality({x \in Updates : baseVersion[x] # 0}) < capacity
              /\ baseVersion' = [baseVersion EXCEPT ![u] = recordVersion + 1]
              /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, recordVersion, capacity, commitVersion>>

\* CAS guard: only a snapshot that is still exactly current+1 may commit,
\* and it writes its own (checked, non-stale) value into recordVersion.
Commit(u) == baseVersion[u] = recordVersion + 1 /\ commitVersion[u] = 0
             /\ recordVersion' = baseVersion[u]
             /\ commitVersion' = [commitVersion EXCEPT ![u] = baseVersion[u]]
             /\ baseVersion' = [baseVersion EXCEPT ![u] = 0]
             /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, capacity>>

\* A stale snapshot (someone else committed meanwhile) is discarded, not
\* applied, so the instruction can retry with a fresh read later.
Abort(u) == baseVersion[u] # 0 /\ baseVersion[u] # recordVersion + 1
            /\ commitVersion[u] = 0
            /\ baseVersion' = [baseVersion EXCEPT ![u] = 0]
            /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, recordVersion, capacity, commitVersion>>

\* Leadership moves; the optimistic guard never depends on who is leader.
Failover(l) == l # leader /\ leader' = l
               /\ UNCHANGED <<recordVersion, capacity, baseVersion, commitVersion>>

CapacityUp == capacity < MaxCapacity /\ capacity' = capacity + 1
              /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, recordVersion, baseVersion, commitVersion>>

CapacityDown == capacity > MinCapacity /\ capacity' = capacity - 1
                /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, recordVersion, baseVersion, commitVersion>>

\* Voluntary withdrawal: unlike Abort (which discards a snapshot that has
\* already gone stale), Withdraw lets an instruction give up a snapshot
\* that is still perfectly fresh (baseVersion[u] = recordVersion + 1) --
\* e.g. a business decision to cancel the settlement before committing it.
\* Its guard is the exact complement of Abort's staleness guard, so the
\* two can never both apply to the same instruction at once.
Withdraw(u) == baseVersion[u] = recordVersion + 1 /\ commitVersion[u] = 0
               /\ baseVersion' = [baseVersion EXCEPT ![u] = 0]
               /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, recordVersion, capacity, commitVersion>>

Next == (\E u \in Updates: Prepare(u)) \/ (\E u \in Updates: Commit(u))
        \/ (\E u \in Updates: Abort(u)) \/ (\E u \in Updates: Withdraw(u))
        \/ (\E l \in Coordinators: Failover(l))
        \/ CapacityUp \/ CapacityDown

vars == <<leader, recordVersion, capacity, baseVersion, commitVersion>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No lost updates: an instruction's own recorded commit version can never
\* be stranded ahead of the record's current version -- if a stale write
\* had ever been let through, it would regress recordVersion below some
\* earlier commitVersion, tripping this.
NoLostUpdates == \A u \in Updates: commitVersion[u] # 0 => commitVersion[u] <= recordVersion
====

CONSTANTS

    InitLeader = l1
    Updates = {u1, u2, u3}
    MinCapacity = 1
    MaxCapacity = 2
    InitCapacity = 1
INVARIANT NoLostUpdates
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A group of banks settle a shared end-of-day net position through a single
settlement coordinator cluster. Exactly one coordinator is the elected leader
at any moment, and leadership can fail over to a different coordinator at any
time (leader election with failover). Each pending settlement instruction
must be folded into one shared settlement record whose optimistic version
number advances by exactly one with every successful update. Because more
than one instruction can be in flight in the coordinator's working set at
once, each instruction first reads (prepares against) the record's current
version before it is allowed to write; it may only actually commit its
result if the version it read is still exactly the record's current version
at the moment it tries to commit. If some other instruction committed in the
meantime, the read is stale and the write must be discarded (aborted) rather
than blindly applied, because applying a write based on a stale version would
silently overwrite -- and thereby lose -- whatever the intervening commit had
already recorded.

The twist is that the coordinator's working capacity -- the maximum number of
instructions that may be simultaneously prepared (holding a read of the
record's version) but not yet committed -- can change at runtime as the
cluster is resized up or down; the safety of the settlement record must not
depend on holding that capacity fixed. Leadership failover is likewise
independent of the per-instruction optimistic check: a change of leader never
resets or forges an instruction's recorded read-version, so the version-based
guard keeps working exactly the same way no matter who is currently leader.

The full action set is:
  - Prepare(u): an instruction u that has not yet committed and is not
    currently holding a read snapshots the settlement record's current
    version, provided the number of instructions currently holding a
    snapshot is below the coordinator's current capacity.
  - Commit(u): an instruction u whose held snapshot exactly equals the
    record's current version plus one writes that snapshot in as the
    record's new version and records that same value as u's commit version,
    releasing its snapshot; this is the only way the shared record's version
    advances.
  - Abort(u): an instruction u whose held snapshot has gone stale (no longer
    equal to the record's current version plus one) because some other
    instruction committed in the meantime releases its snapshot without
    writing anything, so it can retry later with a fresh read.
  - Withdraw(u): an instruction u whose held snapshot is still exactly
    current (equal to the record's current version plus one, i.e. not
    stale) voluntarily gives up that snapshot without committing -- for
    example a business decision to cancel the settlement instruction --
    releasing its snapshot without writing anything. This is distinct from
    Abort: Withdraw only applies to a still-fresh snapshot, Abort only to
    an already-stale one, so the two guards never overlap for the same
    instruction.
  - Failover(l): leadership moves to a different coordinator l; this changes
    only who is recognized as leader and never touches the settlement
    record, capacity, or any instruction's held snapshot.
  - CapacityUp: the coordinator cluster is resized up, raising the maximum
    number of concurrently prepared instructions by one (up to a fixed
    ceiling).
  - CapacityDown: the coordinator cluster is resized down, lowering the
    maximum number of concurrently prepared instructions by one (down to a
    fixed floor).

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every settlement instruction that has ever committed,
the version number it recorded for itself at commit time never exceeds the
settlement record's current version -- no instruction's already-recorded
commit is ever left stranded ahead of the record itself, which is exactly
what would happen if a stale, superseded write were ever allowed through and
silently lost a later instruction's already-applied update.

---- MODULE W4Od3m4p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

\* Banks settle net positions one at a time through a single shared clearing
\* account. Admission is mediated by a bounded FIFO work queue: when the
\* queue is at QueueCap, further enqueues are refused (backpressure). At
\* most one bank may hold the clearing account at once (the mutex the
\* safety invariant protects). One bank may crash silently at any point; a
\* recovery timeout reclaims the account if the crashed bank is the holder,
\* so the queue keeps draining and every other bank still gets served.
CONSTANTS Participants, NoneP, QueueCap

VARIABLES queue, holders, crashed, done

QueueSet(q) == {q[i] : i \in 1..Len(q)}

Init ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ holders = {}
    /\ crashed = NoneP
    /\ done = {}

\* Backpressure: a bank can only enqueue while the queue has room, and only
\* if it is not already queued, holding, done, or the crashed bank.
Enqueue(p) ==
    /\ p # crashed
    /\ p \notin done
    /\ p \notin holders
    /\ p \notin QueueSet(queue)
    /\ Len(queue) < QueueCap
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, p)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holders, crashed, done>>

\* The account is free and the queue non-empty: head of queue is granted
\* exclusive use of the clearing account.
Grant ==
    /\ holders = {}
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ holders' = {Head(queue)}
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, done>>

\* The current holder, if not itself the crashed bank, finishes settling
\* and releases the account.
Complete(p) ==
    /\ p \in holders
    /\ p # crashed
    /\ holders' = holders \ {p}
    /\ done' = done \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed>>

\* Exactly one bank in the consortium silently crashes, at most once ever,
\* and only before it has settled.
Crash ==
    /\ crashed = NoneP
    /\ \E p \in Participants \ done:
         crashed' = p
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, holders, done>>

\* Recovery timeout: if the crashed bank turns out to be the holder,
\* reclaim the account so the queue can keep draining.
Reclaim ==
    /\ crashed # NoneP
    /\ crashed \in holders
    /\ holders' = holders \ {crashed}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, crashed, done>>

Next ==
    \/ (\E p \in Participants: Enqueue(p))
    \/ Grant
    \/ (\E p \in Participants: Complete(p))
    \/ Crash
    \/ Reclaim

vars == <<queue, holders, crashed, done>>

Spec ==
    /\ Init
    /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ (\A p \in Participants: WF_vars(Enqueue(p)))
    /\ WF_vars(Grant)
    /\ (\A p \in Participants: WF_vars(Complete(p)))
    /\ WF_vars(Reclaim)

\* Mutual exclusion of the shared clearing account: never more than one holder.
MutualExclusion == Cardinality(holders) <= 1

\* Every bank is eventually resolved: either it settles, or it turns out to
\* be the one bank that silently crashed.
EveryBankResolved == \A p \in Participants: <>(p \in done \/ crashed = p)
====

    NoneP = none
    QueueCap = 2
INVARIANT MutualExclusion
PROPERTY EveryBankResolved
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A consortium of banks runs a nightly interbank settlement batch. Each participating bank must, in turn, acquire exclusive use of the single shared clearing account (the critical resource that actually posts debits and credits between banks) before it can settle its net position; only one bank may hold the clearing account at a time. Because only a limited number of banks can be mid-flight at once, admission to the clearing account is mediated by a bounded work queue: a bank that wants to settle first enqueues a settlement request, and if the queue is already at its capacity the bank is subject to backpressure and simply cannot enqueue yet -- it must wait for room to open up. When the clearing account is free and the queue is non-empty, the bank at the head of the queue is dequeued and granted exclusive use of the clearing account. Once a bank finishes posting its settlement it releases the clearing account and is marked settled. The twist is that any one bank in the consortium -- whether it is still waiting to enqueue, sitting in the queue, or actively holding the clearing account -- can crash silently at any time before it settles; a crashed bank sends no further messages and never enqueues, completes, or otherwise acts again. To keep the batch from stalling forever, a recovery timeout mechanism watches for this: if the bank currently holding the clearing account turns out to be the crashed one, the timeout fires and reclaims the clearing account on its behalf, freeing it for the next bank in the queue. The system's five actions are: (1) a non-crashed, not-yet-settled bank that is not already queued or holding the account enqueues a settlement request, provided the queue has not reached its capacity bound (backpressure), (2) whenever the clearing account is free and the queue is non-empty, the bank at the head of the queue is granted exclusive use of it, (3) the bank currently holding the clearing account, provided it has not itself silently crashed, finishes settling, releases the account, and is marked settled, (4) exactly one bank in the consortium silently crashes (only if no bank has crashed yet, and only a bank that has not already settled), and (5) if the crashed bank is found to be the current holder of the clearing account, the recovery timeout reclaims the account so the queue can keep draining. SAFETY PROPERTY: at most one bank ever holds exclusive use of the shared clearing account at the same time. LIVENESS PROPERTY: every bank in the consortium is eventually resolved -- it either finishes settling or turns out to be the one bank that silently crashed -- even though the queue enforces backpressure and any single bank may crash silently at any point before it settles.

---- MODULE W4Od3m5p3t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Banks, Slots, Transfers, Quorum, NoTx, AdminBudget

\* Quorum voting normally guards every settlement slot's allocation; a
\* privileged admin can bypass quorum but must do so atomically (replace,
\* never append) so the two paths never together leave a slot double-booked.
VARIABLES proposal, votes, allocations, adminBudget

vars == <<proposal, votes, allocations, adminBudget>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ proposal \in [Slots -> Transfers \cup {NoTx}]
    /\ votes \in [Slots -> SUBSET Banks]
    /\ allocations \subseteq (Slots \X Transfers)
    /\ adminBudget \in 0..AdminBudget

Init ==
    /\ proposal = [s \in Slots |-> NoTx]
    /\ votes = [s \in Slots |-> {}]
    /\ allocations = {}
    /\ adminBudget = AdminBudget

\* A bank starts a fresh voting round on an unallocated, unproposed slot.
Propose(s, t) ==
    /\ proposal[s] = NoTx
    /\ ~ \E tt \in Transfers : <<s, tt>> \in allocations
    /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = t]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<allocations, adminBudget>>

\* A bank not yet counted in this round votes for the slot's live proposal.
Vote(s, b) ==
    /\ proposal[s] # NoTx
    /\ b \notin votes[s]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = @ \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, allocations, adminBudget>>

\* Quorum reached and the slot is still unallocated: commit the record.
Commit(s) ==
    /\ proposal[s] # NoTx
    /\ Cardinality(votes[s]) >= Quorum
    /\ ~ \E tt \in Transfers : <<s, tt>> \in allocations
    /\ allocations' = allocations \cup {<<s, proposal[s]>>}
    /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = NoTx]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED adminBudget

\* Admin spends budget to atomically replace (never append to) a slot's record.
AdminOverride(s, t) ==
    /\ adminBudget > 0
    /\ allocations' = {p \in allocations : p[1] # s} \cup {<<s, t>>}
    /\ adminBudget' = adminBudget - 1
    /\ proposal' = [proposal EXCEPT ![s] = NoTx]
    /\ votes' = [votes EXCEPT ![s] = {}]

\* Admin frees a slot's existing allocation record at no budget cost.
AdminRevoke(s) ==
    /\ \E tt \in Transfers : <<s, tt>> \in allocations
    /\ allocations' = {p \in allocations : p[1] # s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<proposal, votes, adminBudget>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Slots, t \in Transfers : Propose(s, t)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, b \in Banks : Vote(s, b)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Commit(s)
    \/ \E s \in Slots, t \in Transfers : AdminOverride(s, t)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : AdminRevoke(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoDoubleAllocation ==
    \A s \in Slots : Cardinality({t \in Transfers : <<s, t>> \in allocations}) <= 1

====
nl:
A consortium of banks runs a nightly interbank settlement batch. The batch window offers a small fixed set of settlement slots, and each slot may ultimately host at most one settlement transfer. Under normal operation, allocating a slot goes through quorum voting: any bank may propose a transfer for a still-unallocated, currently-unproposed slot, which starts a fresh voting round for that slot (clearing any prior votes). Any bank that has not yet voted in the current round for that slot may then cast a vote for the slot's current proposal. Once a quorum-sized set of distinct banks has voted for a slot's current proposal, and the slot still has no committed allocation record, the proposal is committed: an allocation record binding that slot to that transfer is added, and the slot's proposal/voting state is cleared for the next round.

The twist is that a privileged settlement administrator can override the quorum process entirely. The administrator holds a small, fixed budget of override actions (to keep emergency intervention rare and auditable). Spending one unit of that budget, the administrator may atomically force-allocate any slot to any transfer: this single atomic step first strips out whatever allocation record currently exists for that slot (if any) and then installs the new one, so the override can never leave two records for the same slot behind, and it also resets that slot's in-progress proposal and votes. Separately, and without spending budget, the administrator may revoke an existing allocation record for a slot outright, clearing it back to unallocated so quorum voting (or another override) can allocate it afresh later.

The full action set is therefore: (1) Propose — a bank proposes a transfer for an unproposed, unallocated slot, starting a new voting round; (2) Vote — a bank not yet counted in the current round casts a vote for a slot's current proposal; (3) Commit — once a slot's current proposal has quorum-many votes and the slot is still unallocated, the allocation record is added and the round is cleared; (4) AdminOverride — spending one unit of the admin's override budget, atomically replace whatever allocation record (if any) exists for a slot with a new one for a chosen transfer, and clear that slot's round; (5) AdminRevoke — the administrator deletes an existing allocation record for a slot, freeing it up, at no budget cost.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, for every settlement slot, the set of allocation records bound to that slot contains at most one transfer — no slot is ever simultaneously (or by any sequence of quorum commits and admin overrides) left double-allocated to two different transfers.

---- MODULE W4Od4m2p3t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

\* A car-wash conveyor allocates bay slots via two-phase commit between a
\* track-sensor subsystem and a billing subsystem: both must vote yes on
\* the same proposed slot before the controller commits it to a car. The
\* manager can add or permanently retire slots at runtime; retiring a slot
\* forcibly aborts any in-flight proposal for it. The invariant protects
\* against a slot ever being allocated twice, or allocated after retirement.
CONSTANTS SlotUniverse, InitActive, NoneS

VARIABLES activeSlots, retired, proposedSlot, votes, allocCount

Init ==
    /\ activeSlots = InitActive
    /\ retired = {}
    /\ proposedSlot = NoneS
    /\ votes = {}
    /\ allocCount = [s \in SlotUniverse |-> 0]

\* The controller proposes a free, active, unallocated slot and asks both
\* subsystems to prepare (only one proposal is in flight at a time).
Propose(s) ==
    /\ proposedSlot = NoneS
    /\ s \in activeSlots
    /\ allocCount[s] = 0
    /\ proposedSlot' = s
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<activeSlots, retired, allocCount>>

\* The track-sensor subsystem votes yes on the outstanding proposal.
SensorVote ==
    /\ proposedSlot # NoneS
    /\ "sensor" \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {"sensor"}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<activeSlots, retired, proposedSlot, allocCount>>

\* The billing subsystem votes yes on the outstanding proposal.
BillingVote ==
    /\ proposedSlot # NoneS
    /\ "billing" \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {"billing"}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<activeSlots, retired, proposedSlot, allocCount>>

\* Both subsystems voted yes on the same slot: commit the allocation.
Commit ==
    /\ proposedSlot # NoneS
    /\ votes = {"sensor", "billing"}
    /\ allocCount' = [allocCount EXCEPT ![proposedSlot] = @ + 1]
    /\ proposedSlot' = NoneS
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<activeSlots, retired>>

\* The manager adds a brand-new bay slot to the line.
AddSlot(s) ==
    /\ s \in SlotUniverse \ activeSlots
    /\ s \notin retired
    /\ activeSlots' = activeSlots \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<retired, proposedSlot, votes, allocCount>>

\* The manager permanently retires an active, uncommitted slot; any
\* in-flight proposal for it is aborted and unlocked at both subsystems.
RetireSlot(s) ==
    /\ s \in activeSlots
    /\ allocCount[s] = 0
    /\ retired' = retired \cup {s}
    /\ activeSlots' = activeSlots \ {s}
    /\ IF proposedSlot = s
       THEN proposedSlot' = NoneS /\ votes' = {}
       ELSE proposedSlot' = proposedSlot /\ votes' = votes
    /\ UNCHANGED allocCount

Next ==
    \/ (\E s \in SlotUniverse: Propose(s))
    \/ SensorVote
    \/ BillingVote
    \/ Commit
    \/ (\E s \in SlotUniverse: AddSlot(s))
    \/ (\E s \in SlotUniverse: RetireSlot(s))

vars == <<activeSlots, retired, proposedSlot, votes, allocCount>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No slot is ever allocated more than once, and no retired slot is ever allocated.
SlotSafety ==
    /\ \A s \in SlotUniverse: allocCount[s] <= 1
    /\ \A s \in retired: allocCount[s] = 0
====

nl: A car-wash operates a conveyor line with a fixed set of numbered bay slots that cars move through one at a time. Before a car already queued at the entrance may be conveyed onto a bay slot, the line controller runs a two-phase commit with the two subsystems that jointly guard each slot: the track-sensor subsystem (which confirms the physical bay is actually empty) and the billing subsystem (which confirms the customer's wash package is paid and reserves the charge against that slot). In phase one (prepare) the line controller proposes a specific free slot number to both subsystems, each of which votes yes only if it can independently confirm that exact slot is available from its own point of view, and locks that slot number against further proposals while its vote stands. In phase two, only once both subsystems have voted yes for the same proposed slot does the line controller commit, which is the only way a car is ever actually allocated onto that slot; if instead either subsystem votes no, the controller aborts the proposal for that slot and unlocks it at both subsystems so a different proposal can be made. The twist is that the car wash's manager can change the conveyor's operating capacity at runtime -- adding a brand-new bay slot to the line during a busy period, or permanently retiring an existing bay slot for maintenance -- and a slot that has just been retired must never be the target of a new proposal, must never be committed to, and, if a proposal for it was already in flight, must have that in-flight proposal aborted so the slot cannot be silently allocated to a car after the fact. The system's six actions are: (1) the line controller proposes an uncommitted, unlocked, currently-active slot for the car at the head of the queue, sending prepare requests to both subsystems, (2) the track-sensor subsystem votes yes on an outstanding proposal for a slot it still believes is empty, locking that slot, (3) the billing subsystem votes yes on an outstanding proposal for a slot whose charge it can still reserve, locking that slot, (4) once both subsystems have voted yes on the same proposed slot, the controller commits, allocating that car onto that slot and unlocking it at both subsystems, (5) the manager adds a new bay slot to the line, making it immediately available for future proposals, and (6) the manager retires an existing, uncommitted bay slot, which immediately aborts and unlocks any in-flight proposal for it at both subsystems and removes it from the set of slots that may ever be proposed or committed again. SAFETY PROPERTY: at every reachable state, no bay slot is ever allocated to more than one car at the same time, and no car is ever allocated onto a bay slot that has been retired.

---- MODULE W4Od5m5p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Players, Capacity, NoneP

\* A game lobby matchmaker normally requires a majority-quorum vote among
\* seated players before seating or removing anyone, but a privileged
\* admin can bypass voting entirely. The safety invariant protects the
\* lobby's fixed seat capacity; the liveness property relies on the
\* admin's override (never on the vote succeeding by itself) to guarantee
\* every waiting player is eventually admitted.
VARIABLES seated, queue, candidate, votes

vars == <<seated, queue, candidate, votes>>

Init == seated = {}
        /\ queue = Players
        /\ candidate = NoneP
        /\ votes = {}

ProposeSeat(p) == candidate = NoneP
    /\ p \in queue
    /\ Cardinality(seated) < Capacity
    /\ candidate' = p
    /\ queue' = queue \ {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, votes>>

CastVote(p) == candidate # NoneP
    /\ p \in seated
    /\ p \notin votes
    /\ votes' = votes \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seated, queue, candidate>>

\* A candidate is admitted by ordinary vote only once strictly more than
\* half of the currently seated players have approved it.
AdmitByQuorum == candidate # NoneP
    /\ 2 * Cardinality(votes) > Cardinality(seated)
    /\ Cardinality(seated) < Capacity
    /\ seated' = seated \cup {candidate}
    /\ candidate' = NoneP
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

\* The admin bypasses voting entirely and seats the pending candidate.
AdminForceSeat == candidate # NoneP
    /\ Cardinality(seated) < Capacity
    /\ seated' = seated \cup {candidate}
    /\ candidate' = NoneP
    /\ votes' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED queue

\* The admin can also unilaterally evict any seated player at any time,
\* even mid-vote on an unrelated candidate, freeing a seat for churn.
AdminForceRemove(p) == p \in seated
    /\ seated' = seated \ {p}
    /\ queue' = queue \cup {p}
    /\ votes' = votes \ {p}

        \/ AdmitByQuorum
        \/ AdminForceSeat
        \/ (\E p \in Players : AdminForceRemove(p))

\* ProposeSeat(p) is only intermittently enabled (it is blocked whenever
\* some other candidate is pending), so starvation-freedom for each
\* individual player needs strong fairness, not weak fairness.
Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ (\A p \in Players : SF_vars(ProposeSeat(p)))
        /\ WF_vars(AdminForceSeat)

nl: A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker seats players from a waiting queue into a single match lobby that has a fixed maximum seat capacity. To keep the lobby's roster changes fair, every ordinary seating or removal decision must be approved by a majority-quorum vote among the players already seated in the lobby (a candidate action only takes effect once strictly more than half of the currently seated players have cast an approving vote for it). The lobby also has one privileged admin who can bypass the quorum-voting process entirely and force a seating or removal decision unilaterally at any time, for example to resolve a deadlocked vote or handle an emergency -- this is the twist that lets progress continue even if ordinary voting stalls forever. The full action set is: (1) ProposeSeat -- a player waiting in the queue is proposed as a candidate to be seated next, provided there is no candidate proposal already pending and the lobby currently has fewer seated players than its fixed capacity; (2) CastVote -- a currently seated player who has not yet voted on the pending candidate proposal casts an approving vote for it; (3) AdmitByQuorum -- once strictly more than half of the currently seated players have voted to approve the pending candidate, the candidate moves from the queue into the seated lobby, the capacity is not exceeded, and the pending proposal and its votes are cleared; (4) AdminForceSeat -- the admin unilaterally seats the currently pending candidate (if one is pending) directly into the lobby without needing any votes at all, provided the lobby has fewer seated players than its fixed capacity, clearing the pending proposal and votes; (5) AdminForceRemove -- the admin unilaterally removes any one currently seated player from the lobby back into the waiting queue, without needing any votes, at any time (even mid-vote on an unrelated candidate). SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the number of players seated in the lobby never exceeds the lobby's fixed maximum seat capacity. LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every player who joins the waiting queue is eventually either seated in the lobby or force-seated by the admin -- ordinary voting is never assumed to make progress on its own, but the admin's override guarantees every waiting player is eventually admitted.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m2p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, Floors, NoCar, MaxTerm

\* Two-phase commit assigns each floor call to one car: RequestPrepare bumps
\* a global term and picks a candidate; VoteYes/CoordinatorCommit are the
\* two phases; ServeFloor is the irreversible physical action, gated on the
\* car's recorded vote term still matching the live transaction's term, so
\* a stale or crashed car can never act as an authorized participant.
VARIABLES floorStatus, cand, term, carPreparedTerm, crashedCar

vars == <<floorStatus, cand, term, carPreparedTerm, crashedCar>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ floorStatus \in [Floors -> {"pending", "awaiting-vote", "voted", "committed", "served"}]
    /\ cand \in Cars \cup {NoCar}
    /\ term \in 0..MaxTerm
    /\ carPreparedTerm \in [Cars -> 0..MaxTerm]
    /\ crashedCar \in Cars \cup {NoCar}

Init ==
    /\ floorStatus = [f \in Floors |-> "pending"]
    /\ cand = NoCar
    /\ term = 0
    /\ carPreparedTerm = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
    /\ crashedCar = NoCar

\* Coordinator opens a fresh transaction: picks a pending floor and a live
\* candidate, bumps the term, and sends the prepare request.
RequestPrepare(f, c) ==
    /\ cand = NoCar
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ floorStatus[f] = "pending"
    /\ c # crashedCar
    /\ cand' = c
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ floorStatus' = [floorStatus EXCEPT ![f] = "awaiting-vote"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carPreparedTerm, crashedCar>>

\* The candidate car votes yes and remembers the term it voted for.
VoteYes(c, f) ==
    /\ cand = c
    /\ c # crashedCar
    /\ floorStatus[f] = "awaiting-vote"
    /\ floorStatus' = [floorStatus EXCEPT ![f] = "voted"]
    /\ carPreparedTerm' = [carPreparedTerm EXCEPT ![c] = term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cand, term, crashedCar>>

\* Phase two: coordinator commits on seeing the vote (it cannot itself see
\* a silent crash, so it does not re-check liveness here).
CoordinatorCommit(f) ==
    /\ floorStatus[f] = "voted"
    /\ floorStatus' = [floorStatus EXCEPT ![f] = "committed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<cand, term, carPreparedTerm, crashedCar>>

\* The car performs the irreversible physical service, but only if it is
\* live and its recorded vote is still fresh for the current transaction.
ServeFloor(f) ==
    /\ floorStatus[f] = "committed"
    /\ cand # crashedCar
    /\ carPreparedTerm[cand] = term
    /\ floorStatus' = [floorStatus EXCEPT ![f] = "served"]
    /\ cand' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, carPreparedTerm, crashedCar>>

\* Coordinator times out on a transaction stuck on the known-crashed car.
AbortStalled(f) ==
    /\ floorStatus[f] \in {"awaiting-vote", "voted", "committed"}
    /\ cand = crashedCar
    /\ floorStatus' = [floorStatus EXCEPT ![f] = "pending"]
    /\ cand' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, carPreparedTerm, crashedCar>>

\* Twist: at most one car in the whole bank ever silently crashes.
CrashCar(c) ==
    /\ crashedCar = NoCar
    /\ crashedCar' = c
    /\ UNCHANGED <<floorStatus, cand, term, carPreparedTerm>>

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Floors, c \in Cars : RequestPrepare(f, c)
    \/ \E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : VoteYes(c, f)
    \/ \E f \in Floors : CoordinatorCommit(f)
    \/ \E f \in Floors : ServeFloor(f)
    \/ \E f \in Floors : AbortStalled(f)
    \/ \E c \in Cars : CrashCar(c)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(\E f \in Floors, c \in Cars : RequestPrepare(f, c))
    /\ WF_vars(\E c \in Cars, f \in Floors : VoteYes(c, f))
    /\ WF_vars(\E f \in Floors : CoordinatorCommit(f))
    /\ WF_vars(\E f \in Floors : ServeFloor(f))
    /\ WF_vars(\E f \in Floors : AbortStalled(f))

NoStaleAuthorization ==
    \A f \in Floors :
        floorStatus[f] = "committed" =>
            /\ cand # NoCar
            /\ carPreparedTerm[cand] = term

AllFloorsEventuallyServed == <>(\A f \in Floors : floorStatus[f] = "served")

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2}
    Floors = {f1, f2}
    NoCar = nocar
    MaxTerm = 5
INVARIANT NoStaleAuthorization
PROPERTY AllFloorsEventuallyServed
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper assigns floor-service calls to individual elevator cars using two-phase commit. A coordinator manages, at any one time, at most one active transaction: it picks a still-unserved floor call and a candidate car, bumps a global transaction term, and sends that car a prepare request. The candidate car, if it is still alive, votes yes and records locally the exact term it voted for. Only after seeing that yes vote does the coordinator move the transaction to committed. Only then may the car perform the actual, irreversible physical action of traveling to and opening its doors at that floor, and it may do so only if the term it recorded when it voted still matches the coordinator's current transaction term for that floor — this is what stops a car from ever acting as an unauthorized or stale participant on a transaction that has since moved on without it.

The twist is that exactly one car in the bank may, at any point, crash silently: it simply stops responding to prepare requests and can never again vote or serve a floor, but the coordinator is not immediately told this happened. If the coordinator's current candidate car turns out to be the crashed one, its transaction is permanently stuck (the crashed car will never vote, never get committed for real, and even if it had already been marked committed it will never physically serve the floor) until the coordinator times out on it and aborts, freeing that floor call to be retried later with a different candidate car and a fresh, higher term.

The full action set is: (1) RequestPrepare — the coordinator, with no transaction currently active, below the term budget, picks a still-pending floor and a candidate car that is not the known-crashed one, bumps the global term, and marks that floor's transaction as awaiting that car's vote; (2) VoteYes — the active candidate car, if it has not crashed, votes yes on the floor awaiting its vote and records the current term as the term it voted for; (3) CoordinatorCommit — once a floor's transaction has a recorded yes vote, the coordinator marks it committed, authorizing the candidate car to act (the coordinator does this without itself checking whether the car has meanwhile crashed, since the crash is silent); (4) ServeFloor — the candidate car, if it has not crashed and its recorded voted-term still matches the coordinator's current transaction term, performs the irreversible service action for a committed floor, marking it served and freeing the transaction slot; (5) AbortStalled — if the active transaction's candidate car turns out to be the known-crashed car (whether the transaction is still awaiting a vote, has a vote recorded, or has even been committed), the coordinator aborts it, returning the floor to pending and freeing the transaction slot so a different car can be tried later; (6) CrashCar — the twist: at most one car in the whole bank may, at any point, silently crash and thereafter never vote or serve again.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, whenever a floor's transaction has been marked committed, the recorded candidate car's last-voted term equals the coordinator's current transaction term for that floor — the coordinator never authorizes a car whose vote is stale or who was never a legitimate voting participant of the current transaction.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every floor call is eventually served, even though one car may silently crash mid-transaction, because the coordinator eventually detects and aborts any transaction stuck on the crashed car and retries with a different, live candidate car.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od6m9p6t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT Cars, MaxEpoch

\* An elevator bank's controller reconfigures which cars are authorized to
\* serve calls using an epoch-numbered roster; capacity can grow or shrink
\* at runtime. A car that missed the latest Reconfigure broadcast still
\* remembers an older epoch and must not act on it. The invariant protects
\* against any car serving a call while holding a stale epoch or while it
\* has been dropped from the current roster (an unauthorized, stale act).
VARIABLES epoch, roster, carEpoch, serving, faulty

vars == <<epoch, roster, carEpoch, serving, faulty>>

TypeOK == epoch \in 0..MaxEpoch
          /\ roster \subseteq Cars
          /\ roster # {}
          /\ carEpoch \in [Cars -> 0..MaxEpoch]
          /\ serving \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]
          /\ faulty \in [Cars -> BOOLEAN]

Init == epoch = 0
        /\ roster = Cars
        /\ carEpoch = [c \in Cars |-> 0]
        /\ serving = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]
        /\ faulty = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]

\* The controller bumps the global epoch and installs a fresh authorized
\* roster; the roster must stay non-empty (the bank always keeps at least
\* one car in service) but can otherwise shrink or grow arbitrarily. Any
\* car that was mid-call is forced to a safety stop as part of the same
\* reconfiguration step, since the instant the epoch changes its old
\* authorization is stale -- this is what keeps the invariant meaningful
\* at every state, not only at the instant a call is accepted.
Reconfigure ==
    /\ epoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ \E newRoster \in SUBSET Cars :
         /\ newRoster # {}
         /\ roster' = newRoster
    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ serving' = [c \in Cars |-> FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carEpoch, faulty>>

\* A car finally receives (or catches up on) a Reconfigure broadcast it
\* had missed, adopting the controller's current epoch as its own.
SyncCar ==
    \E c \in Cars :
        /\ carEpoch[c] < epoch
        /\ carEpoch' = [carEpoch EXCEPT ![c] = epoch]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, serving, faulty>>

\* Only a car that is both on the current epoch and currently listed in
\* the roster, and is not reporting a mechanical fault, may begin serving
\* a new passenger call.
AcceptCall ==
    \E c \in Cars :
        /\ carEpoch[c] = epoch
        /\ c \in roster
        /\ ~serving[c]
        /\ ~faulty[c]
        /\ serving' = [serving EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, carEpoch, faulty>>

CompleteCall ==
    \E c \in Cars :
        /\ serving[c]
        /\ serving' = [serving EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, carEpoch, faulty>>

\* A car's own onboard diagnostics detect a mechanical fault at any time,
\* independent of the controller's epoch/roster bookkeeping: this forces
\* an immediate safety stop (if it was mid-call) and blocks it from
\* accepting new calls until maintenance clears the fault.
FlagFault ==
    \E c \in Cars :
        /\ ~faulty[c]
        /\ faulty' = [faulty EXCEPT ![c] = TRUE]
        /\ serving' = [serving EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, carEpoch>>

\* Maintenance clears a car's fault flag, making it eligible again to
\* accept calls (subject to the usual epoch/roster authorization check).
ClearFault ==
    \E c \in Cars :
        /\ faulty[c]
        /\ faulty' = [faulty EXCEPT ![c] = FALSE]
        /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, roster, carEpoch, serving>>

Next == Reconfigure \/ SyncCar \/ AcceptCall \/ CompleteCall
        \/ FlagFault \/ ClearFault

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

NoStaleOrUnauthorizedService ==
    \A c \in Cars : serving[c] => (carEpoch[c] = epoch /\ c \in roster)

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {c1, c2, c3}
    MaxEpoch = 3
INVARIANT NoStaleOrUnauthorizedService
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl: A skyscraper's elevator bank is managed by a building controller that periodically reconfigures which elevator cars are authorized to accept new passenger calls, using an epoch-numbered scheme. Each reconfiguration bumps a global epoch counter and publishes a fresh authorized-car roster for that epoch, because the building's usable elevator capacity changes at runtime (a car can be added to or dropped from service, for example when it goes in for maintenance or comes back online). Each elevator car locally remembers the roster epoch under which it last received authorization to serve calls; a car is only allowed to actually accept and serve a new passenger call if its own remembered epoch matches the controller's current global epoch AND it is listed in that epoch's authorized roster -- a car holding onto a stale, superseded epoch (because it missed the latest Reconfigure broadcast) must never accept new calls, since that would be an unauthorized, stale action. The full action set is: (1) Reconfigure -- the controller bumps the global epoch counter by one and installs a new authorized-car roster (any non-empty subset of the fleet) as the current one, modeling the fleet's capacity changing at runtime; because the instant the epoch changes, any car's prior authorization becomes stale, this same step also forces a safety stop on every car that was mid-call, returning it to idle, so the reconfiguration event itself never leaves a car serving under a now-superseded epoch; (2) SyncCar -- a single car catches up by copying the controller's current epoch number into its own remembered epoch, representing it finally receiving a Reconfigure broadcast it may have missed; (3) AcceptCall -- a car whose remembered epoch equals the controller's current global epoch, and which is listed in the current roster, and which is not already serving a call, and which is not currently reporting a mechanical fault, marks itself as serving a call; (4) CompleteCall -- a car that is currently serving a call finishes it and becomes idle again, still remembering its epoch; (5) FlagFault -- a car's own onboard diagnostics detect a mechanical fault at any time, independent of the controller's epoch/roster bookkeeping, forcing an immediate safety stop if the car was mid-call and marking it faulty so it cannot accept new calls; (6) ClearFault -- building maintenance clears a car's fault flag once repaired, making it eligible again to accept new calls subject to the usual epoch/roster authorization check. Because SyncCar and Reconfigure can interleave arbitrarily and independently per car, some cars can lag behind on stale epochs for an unbounded number of steps while the controller keeps reconfiguring the roster, and independently a car can be flagged faulty at any time regardless of its epoch or roster status. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, every car that is currently serving a passenger call has a remembered epoch equal to the controller's current global epoch and is a member of the current epoch's authorized roster -- no car ever serves a call while holding a stale epoch or while excluded from the current roster.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m0p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Locations, Total, InitLoc, MaxVersion

\* Optimistic locking with retry protects only the contested step (removing
\* a container from a source ledger); reordered pickup/retry messages can
\* never lose or duplicate a container because TotalConserved counts both
\* what is shelved at every location AND what is currently airborne.
VARIABLES count, version, carrying, pending

vars == <<count, version, carrying, pending>>

RECURSIVE SumOver(_, _)
SumOver(f, S) == IF S = {} THEN 0 ELSE
    LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + SumOver(f, S \ {x})

TypeOK ==
    /\ count \in [Locations -> Nat]
    /\ version \in [Locations -> 0..MaxVersion]
    /\ carrying \in [Locations -> Nat]
    /\ pending \subseteq (Locations \X Locations \X (0..MaxVersion))

Init ==
    /\ count = [l \in Locations |-> IF l = InitLoc THEN Total ELSE 0]
    /\ version = [l \in Locations |-> 0]
    /\ carrying = [l \in Locations |-> 0]
    /\ pending = {}

\* A crane snapshots a source's ledger version and files a pickup attempt.
StartPickup(src, dest) ==
    /\ src # dest
    /\ ~ \E r \in pending : r[1] = src /\ r[2] = dest
    /\ pending' = pending \cup {<<src, dest, version[src]>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, version, carrying>>

\* CAS succeeds: source version unchanged since snapshot and stock remains.
CommitPickup(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ LET src == r[1]
           dest == r[2]
           vSnap == r[3]
       IN
        /\ version[src] = vSnap
        /\ count[src] > 0
        /\ version[src] < MaxVersion
        /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![src] = @ - 1]
        /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![src] = @ + 1]
        /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![dest] = @ + 1]
        /\ pending' = pending \ {r}

\* CAS fails: source version moved since the snapshot, so refresh and retry.
RetryAfterConflict(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ LET src == r[1]
           dest == r[2]
           vSnap == r[3]
       IN
        /\ version[src] # vSnap
        /\ pending' = (pending \ {r}) \cup {<<src, dest, version[src]>>}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, version, carrying>>

\* A crane cancels an outstanding pickup attempt without moving anything.
AbandonPickup(r) ==
    /\ r \in pending
    /\ pending' = pending \ {r}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<count, version, carrying>>

\* Delivering an airborne container is a plain addition: it never conflicts.
DropOff(dest) ==
    /\ carrying[dest] > 0
    /\ version[dest] < MaxVersion
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![dest] = @ - 1]
    /\ count' = [count EXCEPT ![dest] = @ + 1]
    /\ version' = [version EXCEPT ![dest] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED pending

Next ==
    \/ \E src, dest \in Locations : StartPickup(src, dest)
    \/ \E r \in pending : CommitPickup(r)
    \/ \E r \in pending : RetryAfterConflict(r)
    \/ \E r \in pending : AbandonPickup(r)
    \/ \E dest \in Locations : DropOff(dest)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TotalConserved == SumOver(count, Locations) + SumOver(carrying, Locations) = Total

====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Locations = {ship, yard, truck}
    Total = 3
    InitLoc = ship
    MaxVersion = 3
INVARIANT TotalConserved
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard moves a fixed number of shipping containers among a small set of storage locations (for example the ship's hold, the yard stack, and a truck chassis). Cranes never create or destroy a container; every container that exists at the start still exists, somewhere, at every later moment. Picking a container up off a location's ledger is protected by optimistic locking with retry, because more than one crane can eye the same source location at once and the network carrying pickup requests and their outcomes can reorder messages relative to each other: a crane first snapshots the source location's ledger version, and only later attempts a compare-and-swap against that snapshot. If the source ledger's version has not moved since the snapshot, the compare-and-swap succeeds and the container is removed from the source's count and becomes airborne, carried by the crane toward its destination; if the version has moved (another crane's pickup or some other update landed first, possibly delivered out of order), the attempt fails and the crane must refresh its snapshot and try again later. Dropping an airborne container off at its destination, by contrast, is a plain addition to the destination's ledger and never conflicts with anything, so it always succeeds once attempted.

The full action set is: (1) StartPickup — a crane, seeing no pickup attempt already outstanding for a given (source, destination) pair, snapshots the source location's current ledger version and files a pickup attempt recording that snapshot; (2) CommitPickup — for an outstanding pickup attempt whose snapshot still matches the source's current ledger version, and while the source still has at least one container, the compare-and-swap succeeds: one container leaves the source's ledger, the source's version is bumped, and the container becomes airborne toward its destination; (3) RetryAfterConflict — for an outstanding pickup attempt whose snapshot no longer matches the source's current ledger version, the crane refreshes the attempt's snapshot to the source's current version so a later compare-and-swap can be tried; (4) AbandonPickup — a crane cancels an outstanding pickup attempt outright, for instance because the job was reassigned, removing it without moving any container; (5) DropOff — a crane holding at least one airborne container destined for a given location delivers one there, adding it to that destination's ledger and bumping that destination's ledger version; this action never fails and needs no snapshot check.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the total number of containers recorded across every location's ledger plus every container currently airborne between locations equals the fixed total number of containers the yard started with — no container is ever created or destroyed by any sequence of pickups, retries, or drop-offs, however the underlying messages were reordered.

spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od7m4p5t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Cranes, Containers, QueueCap, NoneC

\* The dispatch queue is a bounded work queue with backpressure (QueueCap).
\* loadCount tracks, per container, how many times it has actually been
\* loaded -- the irreversible action the invariant protects. A crashed
\* crane freezes with its container attached; Reassign is the only way to
\* free that container, and it only fires before the container is loaded,
\* so reassignment can never itself cause a double load.
VARIABLES waiting, queued, bounced, inProgress, loadCount, crashedCrane

TypeOK == waiting \subseteq Containers /\ queued \subseteq Containers
          /\ bounced \subseteq Containers
          /\ inProgress \in [Containers -> Cranes \cup {NoneC}]
          /\ loadCount \in [Containers -> Nat]
          /\ crashedCrane \in Cranes \cup {NoneC}

Init == waiting = Containers /\ queued = {} /\ bounced = {}
        /\ inProgress = [k \in Containers |-> NoneC]
        /\ loadCount = [k \in Containers |-> 0]
        /\ crashedCrane = NoneC

Submit(k) == k \in waiting /\ Cardinality(queued) < QueueCap
             /\ waiting' = waiting \ {k} /\ queued' = queued \cup {k}
             /\ UNCHANGED <<bounced, inProgress, loadCount, crashedCrane>>

Bounce(k) == k \in waiting /\ Cardinality(queued) = QueueCap
             /\ waiting' = waiting \ {k} /\ bounced' = bounced \cup {k}
             /\ UNCHANGED <<queued, inProgress, loadCount, crashedCrane>>

Retry(k) == k \in bounced /\ Cardinality(queued) < QueueCap
            /\ bounced' = bounced \ {k} /\ queued' = queued \cup {k}
            /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, inProgress, loadCount, crashedCrane>>

Assign(cr, k) == cr # crashedCrane /\ k \in queued
                 /\ (\A k2 \in Containers: inProgress[k2] # cr)
                 /\ inProgress' = [inProgress EXCEPT ![k] = cr]
                 /\ queued' = queued \ {k}
                 /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, bounced, loadCount, crashedCrane>>

Load(cr, k) == cr # crashedCrane /\ inProgress[k] = cr /\ loadCount[k] = 0
               /\ loadCount' = [loadCount EXCEPT ![k] = loadCount[k] + 1]
               /\ inProgress' = [inProgress EXCEPT ![k] = NoneC]
               /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, queued, bounced, crashedCrane>>

\* Exactly one crane, ever, may crash silently, freezing its cargo in place.
Crash(cr) == crashedCrane = NoneC /\ crashedCrane' = cr
             /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, queued, bounced, inProgress, loadCount>>

\* A container stuck on the crashed crane, not yet loaded, goes back to the
\* dispatch queue for another crane to finish the job.
Reassign(k) == crashedCrane # NoneC /\ inProgress[k] = crashedCrane
               /\ loadCount[k] = 0
               /\ inProgress' = [inProgress EXCEPT ![k] = NoneC]
               /\ queued' = queued \cup {k}
               /\ UNCHANGED <<waiting, bounced, loadCount, crashedCrane>>

LeaveWaiting(k) == Submit(k) \/ Bounce(k)
AssignAny(k) == \E cr \in Cranes: Assign(cr, k)
LoadAny(k) == \E cr \in Cranes: Load(cr, k)

Next == (\E k \in Containers: Submit(k)) \/ (\E k \in Containers: Bounce(k))
        \/ (\E k \in Containers: Retry(k))
        \/ (\E cr \in Cranes, k \in Containers: Assign(cr, k))
        \/ (\E cr \in Cranes, k \in Containers: Load(cr, k))
        \/ (\E cr \in Cranes: Crash(cr))
        \/ (\E k \in Containers: Reassign(k))

vars == <<waiting, queued, bounced, inProgress, loadCount, crashedCrane>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars
        /\ (\A k \in Containers: WF_vars(LeaveWaiting(k)))
        /\ (\A k \in Containers: SF_vars(Retry(k)))
        /\ (\A k \in Containers: SF_vars(AssignAny(k)))
        /\ (\A k \in Containers: WF_vars(LoadAny(k)))
        /\ (\A k \in Containers: WF_vars(Reassign(k)))

\* SAFETY: the irreversible load action fires at most once per container.
AtMostOnceLoaded == \A k \in Containers: loadCount[k] <= 1

\* LIVENESS: every container is eventually loaded, exactly once.
AllEventuallyLoaded == <>(\A k \in Containers: loadCount[k] = 1)
====

SPECIFICATION Spec
CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {cr1, cr2}
    Containers = {k1, k2, k3}
    QueueCap = 2
    NoneC = none
INVARIANT AtMostOnceLoaded
PROPERTY AllEventuallyLoaded
CHECK_DEADLOCK FALSE
nl:
A container-ship crane yard runs a small pool of gantry cranes that load
containers onto a departing ship. Every container destined for the ship must
first pass through a bounded dispatch queue before a crane can pick it up:
the dispatcher can hold at most QueueCap containers waiting for a crane at
once. A container whose turn to enter the dispatch queue comes up while the
queue is already full is bounced by backpressure and marked as bounced; a
bounced container must be resubmitted later once the queue has room again.
Once a container reaches the front of the dispatch queue, an idle crane (one
not already carrying another container) picks it up. Loading a container
onto the ship is irreversible -- once a crane has actually swung a given
container aboard, that specific container can never be loaded a second time.

The twist is that a crane can crash silently while it is carrying a
container it has picked up but not yet loaded. A crashed crane freezes
exactly where it was -- it never loads its container and never picks up
another one. To keep the yard moving, a reassignment step notices when a
container is still attached to a crashed crane and returns that container to
the dispatch queue so a different, working crane can pick it up and load it;
reassignment only ever happens to a container that has not yet been loaded,
so it can never cause a container to be loaded twice.

The full action set is:
  - Submit(k): a waiting container k enters the dispatch queue, provided the
    queue currently has room under QueueCap.
  - Bounce(k): a waiting container k arrives while the queue is full, so it
    is bounced by backpressure instead of queued.
  - Retry(k): a previously bounced container k re-enters the dispatch queue
    once the queue has room again.
  - Assign(cr, k): an idle, non-crashed crane cr picks up container k from
    the front of the dispatch queue.
  - Load(cr, k): crane cr, currently carrying container k, irreversibly
    loads k onto the ship; this can only ever happen once per container.
  - Crash(cr): at most one crane, chosen nondeterministically, crashes
    silently while carrying whatever container it currently holds (if any).
  - Reassign(k): a container k still attached to a crashed crane, and not
    yet loaded, is returned to the dispatch queue so another crane can take
    it over.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No container is ever loaded onto the ship more than once --
for every container, the number of times it has been loaded never exceeds
one.
LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every container that starts out waiting for the dispatch
queue is eventually loaded onto the ship exactly once, even though it may
first be bounced by backpressure and even though the crane that first picks
it up may crash silently before loading it.

---- MODULE W4Od8m1p0t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

\* A university course-registration ledger is protected by a single token
\* circulating around registration terminals in a fixed ring. Only the
\* current token holder may write. At most one terminal ever crashes,
\* silently; if it crashes while holding the token, the token is lost, and
\* any live terminal may mint a fresh (higher-epoch) replacement so the
\* ring can resume without the crashed terminal ever writing again.

CONSTANTS N, NoneP, InitHolder

\* Terminals are numbered 1..N and sit on a fixed ring; NoneP (0) means
\* "no token currently exists".
Participants == 1..N
Ring == [p \in Participants |-> IF p = N THEN 1 ELSE p + 1]

VARIABLES holder, epoch, crashed, inCS, requesting

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in Participants \cup {NoneP}
    /\ epoch \in Nat
    /\ crashed \subseteq Participants
    /\ inCS \subseteq Participants
    /\ requesting \subseteq Participants

Init ==
    /\ holder = InitHolder
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ inCS = {}
    /\ requesting = {}

\* A live terminal that isn't already waiting asks for ledger access.
Request ==
    /\ \E p \in Participants \ crashed :
        /\ p \notin requesting
        /\ requesting' = requesting \cup {p}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, crashed, inCS>>

\* The live token holder, if it has an outstanding request, opens the ledger.
EnterLedger ==
    /\ holder # NoneP
    /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ holder \in requesting
    /\ inCS' = inCS \cup {holder}
    /\ requesting' = requesting \ {holder}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, epoch, crashed>>

\* The writing terminal closes the ledger and hands the token onward,
\* skipping a crashed immediate successor (at most one terminal ever
\* crashes, so the successor's successor is guaranteed still live).
ExitLedger ==
    /\ \E p \in inCS :
        /\ inCS' = inCS \ {p}
        /\ holder' = IF Ring[p] \in crashed THEN Ring[Ring[p]] ELSE Ring[p]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, crashed, requesting>>

\* At most one terminal, ever, crashes silently; it is scrubbed from the
\* ledger and from pending requests, and the token is lost if it held it.
CrashTerminal ==
    /\ crashed = {}
    /\ \E p \in Participants :
        /\ crashed' = {p}
        /\ inCS' = inCS \ {p}
        /\ requesting' = requesting \ {p}
        /\ holder' = IF holder = p THEN NoneP ELSE holder
    /\ UNCHANGED epoch

\* A lost token can be replaced by any still-live terminal, one epoch newer.
RegenerateToken ==
    /\ holder = NoneP
    /\ crashed # {}
    /\ \E p \in Participants \ crashed :
        /\ holder' = p
        /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, inCS, requesting>>

Next == Request \/ EnterLedger \/ ExitLedger \/ CrashTerminal \/ RegenerateToken

vars == <<holder, epoch, crashed, inCS, requesting>>

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* SAFETY: mutual exclusion on the ledger, and no crashed terminal ever
\* writes to it or is trusted with the token.
MutualExclusion ==
    /\ Cardinality(inCS) <= 1
    /\ crashed \cap inCS = {}
    /\ (holder # NoneP) => holder \notin crashed

====

    NoneP = 0

INVARIANT MutualExclusion

nl:
A university's course-registration system lets a fixed set of registration terminals write to a single shared enrollment ledger (the resource that actually commits seat assignments). Exclusive write access to the ledger is granted by a single circulating token that moves around the terminals in a fixed ring order (each terminal has one designated next-terminal in the ring). Only the terminal currently holding the token may open the ledger for writing; when it is done it closes the ledger and passes the token on to the next terminal in the ring. One terminal can crash silently at any point -- if it crashes while holding the token, the token is lost with it (the ring stalls) rather than being cleanly handed off; if it crashes while merely waiting, it simply stops participating. Once the token is lost because its holder crashed, any other still-live terminal may mint a freshly numbered replacement token for itself so registration can eventually resume, but a crashed terminal itself may never again request access, hold the token, or write to the ledger.

The system's actions are: (1) Request -- a live (non-crashed) terminal that is not already waiting marks itself as wanting ledger access; (2) EnterLedger -- the terminal currently holding the token, if it is live and has an outstanding request, opens the ledger for writing (enters the critical section); (3) ExitLedger -- a terminal that is writing to the ledger closes it and hands the token to the next terminal in the fixed ring order, skipping over that next terminal if it has crashed (since at most one terminal ever crashes, the terminal after that is guaranteed still live); (4) CrashTerminal -- a designated terminal (at most one, ever) crashes silently: it is marked crashed, is immediately removed from the ledger and from any outstanding request, and if it was the token holder the token becomes lost; (5) RegenerateToken -- when the token is lost and at least one terminal has crashed, some still-live terminal mints a freshly numbered token for itself so the ring can resume operating without the crashed terminal.

SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, at most one terminal is writing to the shared enrollment ledger at a time, no crashed terminal is ever writing to the ledger, and the token (when it exists) is never held by a crashed terminal.

---- MODULE W4Od8m1p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANT NumServers, Total, NoneS

\* A token circulates around a ring of campus registration servers; only
\* the current token holder may move course seats between the shared open
\* pool and its own local reserved pool. A server can crash silently at
\* any moment, even while holding the token, so the ring must route the
\* token around dead servers and never leave it stranded. The invariant
\* protects the fixed total seat count against ever being lost or
\* duplicated as seats move back and forth under exclusive token control.
Servers == 1..NumServers

VARIABLES crashed, holder, openPool, reserved

vars == <<crashed, holder, openPool, reserved>>

RECURSIVE SumReserved(_)
SumReserved(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
                  ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
                       IN reserved[s] + SumReserved(S \ {s})

\* Walks the ring starting just after s, skipping crashed servers, until
\* it finds a survivor. Bounded by NumServers steps since s itself (the
\* current holder, always non-crashed when this is invoked) is reached
\* again after a full lap if nobody else survives.
RECURSIVE NextAliveFrom(_, _)
NextAliveFrom(s, k) ==
    LET cand == ((s + k - 1) % NumServers) + 1
    IN IF cand \notin crashed THEN cand ELSE NextAliveFrom(s, k + 1)

NextAlive(s) == NextAliveFrom(s, 1)

Init == crashed = {}
        /\ holder = 1
        /\ openPool = Total
        /\ reserved = [s \in Servers |-> 0]

CrashServer == \E s \in Servers :
    s \notin crashed
    /\ crashed' = crashed \cup {s}
    /\ \/ /\ holder = s
          /\ holder' = NoneS
       \/ /\ holder # s
          /\ holder' = holder
    /\ UNCHANGED <<openPool, reserved>>

PassToken == \E s \in Servers :
    holder = s /\ s \notin crashed
    /\ holder' = NextAlive(s)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, openPool, reserved>>

RecoverToken == holder = NoneS
    /\ \E s \in Servers :
         s \notin crashed
         /\ holder' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, openPool, reserved>>

ClaimSeat == holder # NoneS /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ openPool > 0
    /\ openPool' = openPool - 1
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![holder] = @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, holder>>

ReleaseSeat == holder # NoneS /\ holder \notin crashed
    /\ reserved[holder] > 0
    /\ openPool' = openPool + 1
    /\ reserved' = [reserved EXCEPT ![holder] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<crashed, holder>>

Next == CrashServer \/ PassToken \/ RecoverToken \/ ClaimSeat \/ ReleaseSeat

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

SeatsConserved == openPool + SumReserved(Servers) = Total

====

INVARIANT SeatsConserved

nl: A university course-registration system controls exclusive write access to one course's seat inventory using a token that circulates around a fixed ring of registration servers (one per campus). Only the server currently holding the token is allowed to move seats between the "open" pool of unclaimed seats for the course and a server's local pool of seats it has reserved for students at its own campus; this prevents two campuses from double-booking the same physical seats. Because a registration server can crash silently at any moment -- it stops responding and never sends or receives anything again, with no warning to the rest of the ring -- the ring must be able to route around a dead server, and the token must still make it safely to the next surviving server rather than being lost forever inside a dead one. The full action set is: (1) CrashServer -- one non-crashed server crashes silently, and if it happened to be holding the token, the token is simply gone until the next action recovers it (recorded in a crashed-servers set, no other change); (2) PassToken -- the server currently holding the token, provided it has not crashed, passes it along the ring to the next server after it that has not crashed, skipping over any crashed servers in between; (3) RecoverToken -- if the server that was holding the token crashed while holding it (so no server currently holds the token), any one non-crashed server may take up the orphaned token and become the new holder, so the token is never lost forever; (4) ClaimSeat -- the server currently holding the (non-crashed) token moves one seat from the shared open pool into its own local reserved pool, provided the open pool has at least one seat available; (5) ReleaseSeat -- the server currently holding the (non-crashed) token moves one seat back from its own local reserved pool into the shared open pool, provided its local reserved pool has at least one seat. Seats only ever move between the shared open pool and a server's local reserved pool, one at a time, under exclusive control of whichever server holds the token, so the total number of seats for the course never changes no matter how servers crash, how the token circulates, or how many claims and releases happen. SAFETY PROPERTY: At every reachable state, the shared open pool's seat count plus the sum of every server's local reserved pool seat count equals the fixed total number of seats the course started with.
